Warning: this article contains spoilers for Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey.

In Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, Odysseus (played by Matt Damon) is lost not only at sea, but within his own memories. On the island of the nymph Calypso (Charlize Theron), eating lotus flowers offers him relief from the trauma of Troy, allowing him to forget the war, his comrades – and eventually even his wife and son.

While it’s a point of focus in Nolan’s film, the episode of the so-called “Lotus eaters” is, in the scheme of Homer’s Odyssey, very minor. Occupying scarcely more than 20 lines of verse in a poem of over 12,000, the story of the magical, memory-wiping fruit is no more than an unfortunate escapade.

open image in gallery Odysseus (played by Matt Damon) is lost not only at sea, but within his own memories ( Universal Pictures )

The cyclops, in the economy of the poem, is far more significant. The famous trick, by which Odysseus makes the cyclops believe he is called “Nobody”, rendering the creature’s cries for help useless (“Nobody is attacking me!”), encourages Odysseus, at a safe distance, to reveal his name. The cyclops’ subsequent curse becomes a major motive force for the rest of the poem.

Christopher Nolan’s new film adaptation of the Odyssey has reversed this. Although the cyclops still represents the clash of civilisation and brutishness, the episode in the film is relegated to a symptom of a wider problem.

When finally reunited with his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway), Odysseus confesses his guilt over the destruction of Troy. To trick a people into accepting a gift – the Trojan horse – which spells their doom, in the name of the goddess Athena, is to violate the divine sanctions that keep human behaviour decent. If the cyclops does not know “the laws of Zeus” (in Greek, xenia: the bonds of behaviour between guest and host), what of it? The Trojan war has collapsed any meaning these notions once had anyway.

open image in gallery When finally reunited with his wife, Penelope (Anne Hathaway), Odysseus confesses his guilt over the destruction of Troy ( Universal Pictures )

Into the gap steps the lotus – in Nolan’s film it’s a flower, and not a fruit as in Homer’s poem. In Nolan’s film, the magic flower is used by Calypso to purge Odysseus’ trauma. What she unleashes is, however, a crippling addiction. Only through painstaking narrative can Odysseus slowly piece together the memory of his men, and only by touching an artefact from his past can his memory of his wife be restored. The whole first half of the film, then, is a lotus-induced dream.

The traumatic Odyssey

How are we to handle memories we do not like? If you could remove them, would you? For many, memories are so painful that chemical remedies are sought.

Among UK veterans of combat, 11% have reported alcohol misuse problems. In the US, some million veterans suffer from addictions to alcohol or drugs.

Nolan’s Odysseus is a commentary on this. Confronted with a world he has played a pivotal role in destroying, Odysseus loses himself in lotus addiction. Calypso’s motives are left tantalisingly ambiguous. Part nursemaid, part temptress (but somewhat sexless in comparison with Homer’s version), she regulates the supply of the drug she has introduced him to (we see her both encourage and forbid the use of lotus).

About the author Ben Cartlidge is a Lecturer in Greek Culture and Classical Receptions, University of Liverpool.This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

Both forgetting and memory have their pitfalls. Neither the bitterness of dwelling on a lost past, nor the blanking out of suffering, are the same as healing. In Homer’s Odyssey, a pivotal moment features Odysseus listening to a singer tell the story of the Trojan war at a banquet. It’s the only time Homer actually mentions the notorious wooden horse. Much is made of Odysseus’ response: he covers his face and he weeps. The song of the Sirens too introduces Odysseus to pain and regret, to memory both lost and betrayed.

In the film, unlike the poem, narrative therapy – the telling of the tale – does not suffice. The solution is rather the rediscovery of powerlessness – of a small human’s place in a vast world. Nolan’s Odysseus is a figure of controlling power, whether successfully, in the case of the attack on the Cyclops, or unsuccessfully, as Circe (Samantha Morton) implies when his men raid her home. Research has found that surf therapy can help veterans suffering with PTSD. In a similar way, Odysseus’s trauma is healed by understanding, and yielding to, what he cannot control after all.

Odysseus is described by Homer in the first line of the poem as polutropos: “of many turns”, “complicated”, “resourceful” – the word is notoriously untranslatable. Whatever this means, in Nolan’s imagination, Odysseus is not a warrior. He is a culture hero – a figure who changes the world – and it is responsibility for the downfall of a culture which has marked him with trauma.

News.title: Salman Rushdie’s attacker goes on trial again in federal case centered on decades-old ‘fatwa’
News.content:

The man convicted of trying to kill author Salman Rushdie is on trial again, this time in a federal case that casts the stabbing on a lecture stage as an act of terrorism.

Prosecutors say Hadi Matar attacked the renowned author and free-speech advocate in 2022 to try to carry out a decades-old fatwa, or religious ruling, calling for Rushdie's death over what some Muslims saw as blasphemy in his 1988 novel The Satanic Verses.

“Fulfill the fatwa — that’s what Hadi Matar intended to do,” Assistant U.S. Attorney Timothy Lynch said in an opening statement at a federal courthouse in Buffalo, New York, about 70 miles (110 km) from the arts and intellectual retreat where Rushdie was assaulted. The Booker Prize-winning author is expected to testify later this week about the stabbing that nearly killed him and left him blind in one eye.

Prosecutors said Matar's writings, communications and other materials showed he acted out of loyalty to Iran’s theocratic government and the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group; Iran's late Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini issued the fatwa.

Defense attorney Nathaniel Barone urged jurors to keep their minds open.

open image in gallery Prosecutors say Hadi Matar attacked the renowned author and free-speech advocate in 2022 to try to carry out a decades-old fatwa, or religious ruling ( AP Photo/Adrian Kraus )

“You’re going to have to ask yourselves: What was Hadi Matar’s intent?” Barone said in his opening. "The government doesn’t know what Hadi intends or what his state of mind was at any time, quite frankly.”

An audience watched in terror as Rushdie was stabbed

Matar, 28, has pleaded not guilty to federal charges that include engaging in an act of transnational terrorism. Currently serving a 25-year New York State prison sentence on an attempted murder and assault conviction, he was attired for court in dress pants and a shirt that seemed too large.

After opening statements, jurors saw video of the attack. It unfolded in front of a horrified audience at the Chautauqua Institution, where Rushdie was about to discuss writer safety.

His assailant, wearing a medical mask, strode onstage and stabbed Rushdie repeatedly, continuing even as the writer got up and fell backward. Spectators rushed to pull the attacker off Rushdie and held the assailant face-down until a state trooper arrived.

As one of the videos played, Matar, 28, placed his head down on the defense table several times before looking back up at the screen. Otherwise, he spent much of the time writing notes on a yellow pad and exchanged comments with his lawyers.

Rushdie, now 79, has recounted the assault and his lengthy recovery during Matar's earlier trial, in a memoir and in multiple interviews.

“The thing that happens when you get really a close-up look at death — that’s as close as you can get without actually doing the dance of death and heading off to nowhere — it stays with you,” he told The Associated Press in 2024. “There’s a shadow.”

Federal terrorism trial hinges on Matar's motivation

The attempted murder case against Matar focused on the details of the knife attack while the federal one delves more into questions of motive. If convicted, he faces a potential life sentence.

Matar kept a journal and sticky notes logging his years of research on Rushdie — including the location of his office, the sports teams he followed and establishments where he sometimes watched games, Lynch said in his opening statement.

“We need to kill him ASAP,” Matar wrote, framing the killing as part of what he considered a jihad, or holy war, according to the prosecutor. He said Matar added: “Become a warrior and just get it over with.”

open image in gallery A courtroom sketch shows Matar seated with his lawyer's co-council as a witness describes video of the attack on Salman Rushdie ( AP )

In Matar’s New Jersey bedroom, federal agents found photos of Khomeini, his now-deceased successor Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, and a Hezbollah figure, Lynch said. Matar's computer held a photo of him saluting in a Hezbollah-related t-shirt, plus a video about the fatwa that sought Rushdie's death, and Matar asked a contact in 2022 whether the edict was still valid, the prosecutor said.

On the day of the attack, Matar carried a fake driver's license in a Hezbollah figure's name, prosecutors said.

“The defendant wanted everyone to know he was doing this for Hezbollah," Lynch told jurors.

Matar declined to testify at his state court trial, and it's unclear whether he will take the stand in federal court. At his state court sentencing, Matar said he believed in free speech but that Rushdie was “a hypocrite” and a “bully.”

Matar also spoke out in support of Palestinians while heading into and out of the state courtroom.

Born in the U.S. to parents who immigrated from Lebanon, Matar is a citizen of both countries. His mother has said he turned moody and withdrawn after a 2018 trip to Lebanon, where Hezbollah is based.

How Ayatollah's edict affected Rushdie

Rushdie was born in India, raised in Britain — where he was knighted by the late Queen Elizabeth II — and is now a U.S. citizen. He won the Booker Prize in 1981 for Midnight’s Children, a magical realist novel about a personal and national journey that begins at the instant when India became independent.

But Rushdie became most famous, and notorious, for The Satanic Verses, particularly a passage featuring a dream sequence about the Prophet Muhammad. Often-violent protests erupted against Rushdie, who was born into a Muslim family.

Khomeini's 1989 fatwa drove Rushdie into hiding for years. Although Iran hasn't focused in recent years on the decree, it was never rescinded. Iran's government denied involvement in the 2022 stabbing, but its Foreign Ministry's then-spokesperson suggested Rushdie invited trouble by insulting Islam.

After Knife, Rushdie's memoir about the stabbing, he returned to fiction with last year's The Eleventh Hour, a book of short stories and novellas. He was recognized with a Dayton Literary Peace Prize lifetime achievement award in November.

The popular prediction market Kalshi has unveiled a midterm elections hub, claiming that trading on its exchange will provide “an always-on, real-time picture” of the fight for control of Congress in November.

"Prediction markets don't care about spin or partisanship. They cut through polarization and show you what the wisdom of the crowds actually believes, backed by real money, not rhetoric," Tarek Mansour, co-founder and CEO of Kalshi, said in a statement. "That kind of clarity is rare right now and that's what people are getting with the Midterms Hub."

The hub includes markets regarding the overall control of Congress, individual high-profile races and more obscure fights such as local mayoral elections and ballot initiatives.

Kalshi argues the information gained from its site is superior to traditional political polling, writing in an announcement about the hub that “a poll is a static snapshot, while a market is a living forecast of the future.”

Kalshi competitor Polymarket has a similar elections hub.

open image in gallery Prediction markets Kalshi and Polymarket have midterm elections hubs where traders have spent hundreds of millions of dollars predicting the winners of the November races ( Getty )

Traders on both exchanges have spent nearly $200 million betting on the 2026 elections so far, according to a recent NBC News analysis.

Their predictions have at times diverged from mainstream poll-tracking.

Race to the WH, one popular poll aggregator, has Democrats likelier to win the Senate majority, while Polymarket bettors largely think the GOP has a better chance.

Despite considerable enthusiasm around political prediction markets, their mainstream adoption has also raised corruption concerns.

One of President Donald Trump’s teleprompter operators was put on unpaid administrative leave after being accused of winning more than $100,000 from betting on the content of the president’s speeches.

Gabriel Perez is currently complying with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt confirmed Thursday.

open image in gallery The president’s son Donald Trump Jr. advises both Polymarket and Kalshi ( AFP/Getty )

Leavitt added that the president found the situation “deeply unfortunate and frankly a disgrace.”

In March, the White House reportedly warned staffers against using nonpublic information to make political bets, after a trio of Polymarket accounts made more than $600,000 accurately predicting the timing of a ceasefire in the Iran war.

Earlier, in 2024, U.S. Rep. Anna Paulina Luna of Florida allegedly tipped off a MAGA influencer, Rogan O’Handley, that Donald Trump would choose JD Vance as his running mate, teeing up a winning bet on Polymarket, The Wall Street Journal reported.

The alleged tip and trade reportedly inspired an investigation from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission.

open image in gallery One of President Donald Trump’s teleprompter operators was put on unpaid administrative leave after being accused of winning more than $100,000 from betting on the content of the president’s speeches ( Reuters )

Luna and O’Handley have strongly denied any wrongdoing, and Luna’s office previously told The Independent she has “filed a complaint with the CTFC which has now opened a criminal investigation” based on an individual making false and defamatory claims about her.

The president’s son Donald Trump Jr. advises both Polymarket and Kalshi. His venture capital firm is also an investor in Polymarket.

Both Kalshi and Polymarket say they monitor and flag illegal activity on their platforms.

States across the country have sued both exchanges, arguing they are illegally operating without gambling licenses.

The companies argue they are not conducting gambling but rather engaged in legal, federally regulated contract and prediction markets.

News.title: D4vd’s money manager knew victim’s first name before body was found, court hears
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A money manager for singer D4vd testified Wednesday that he knew only Celeste Rivas Hernandez’s first name before the 14-year-old’s dismembered body was discovered in the trunk of a car.

Benjamin Gregor’s testimony came during the second day of a Los Angeles preliminary hearing, where a judge is weighing whether there is enough evidence to send D4vd, whose legal name is David Burke, to trial on charges including murder, continuous sexual abuse of a child under 14 and mutilation of human remains.

“I knew her first name,” Gregor testified.

Prosecutors later asked Gregor how he learned the name Celeste. He said it came from D4vd’s manager, Rob Morgenroth. When Deputy District Attorney Beth Silverman asked whether Morgenroth had told him Celeste was D4vd’s girlfriend, objections prevented him from answering.

open image in gallery Burke’s lawyers have said he did not cause Rivas Hernandez’s death, and he has pleaded not guilty to the charges ( Bill Robles via AP )

Burke’s lawyers have said he did not cause Rivas Hernandez’s death, and he has pleaded not guilty to the charges. Prosecutors allege Burke fatally stabbed Rivas Hernandez to prevent her from revealing their relationship and ruining his career.

Gregor was one of two witnesses called to discuss Burke’s finances, to indicate how much he had to lose, and whether the killing could have meant financial gain.

But the questioning, which got increasingly heated, swerved into who among the people around Burke knew he was in a sexual relationship with the teen.

Silverman asked Gregor if he knew Burke had taken Rivas Hernandez to London with him, and to Texas to meet his family. He said he had heard about the London trip.

The prosecutor asked if he had heard about Burke taking Rivas Hernandez to nightclubs, with both of them using fake IDs. Burke only recently turned 21.

This drew angry objections from Burke's attorney, Marilyn Bednarski.

“Counsel is testifying!” she said.

Judge Charlaine F. Olmedo, who will decide whether there is probable cause for trial, cut off the line of questioning.

open image in gallery Prosecutors are seeking to prove that Burke met Rivas Hernandez when she was 11 and began a sexual relationship with her when she was 13 and he was 18 ( Ted Soqui/Getty Images )

Prosecutors are seeking to prove that Burke, an indie-pop singer whose music and online presence brought him a huge following, met Rivas Hernandez when she was 11 and began a sexual relationship with her when she was 13 and he was 18.

They said in a court filing that she had grown jealous of his relationships with other women and threatened to expose him.

The court filing said Burke sent a car to pick up Rivas Hernandez on April 23, 2025, from her hometown of Lake Elsinore, California, some 80 miles (129 km) outside Los Angeles. They exchanged messages until she arrived at his home, after which her phone went dead. Prosecutors say he stabbed her when she arrived.

Tuesday's first day of the preliminary hearing focused largely on what came after her death.

The lead investigator, Los Angeles police homicide detective Joshua Byers, testified that records showed Burke had ordered a body bag, chain saws, an inflatable pool and a shovel online, and most of the items were found in Burke's garage when a search warrant was served.

Prosecutors say he dismembered her body in the garage, and kept it in the front trunk of his Tesla, where it was found after the car was towed 4 1/2 months later in September.

Byers testified that when he was called to the Hollywood tow yard, a body bag matching the one Burke had ordered contained a head and torso, with arms and legs underneath in garbage bags.

Photos of the body in the open trunk were shown in court as her parents, Jesus Rivas and Mercedes Martinez, sat in the audience. The two were back in the courtroom on Wednesday. They are not expected to testify at the hearing.

The defendant, who has been held without bail since his arrest, appeared in court in his orange jail clothes and glasses.

The financial witnesses testified that Burke's music had earned him at least $10 million between 2023 and 2025.

Under the name D4vd (pronounced “David”), he began writing and recording songs for YouTube videos he created of the video game Fortnite as a teen.

The music was a blend of indie rock, R&B and lo-fi pop. The music made him a phenomenon on TikTok, Soundcloud and Spotify, where his top songs, including his 2022 breakthrough “Romantic Homicide,” have more than a billion plays.

In 2023, he released two EPs and opened for SZA on tour. Last year, he performed at the Coachella music festival and released a full album that he was on tour promoting when the body was discovered.

A New York City woman is suing McDonald’s after allegedly sustaining “serious and severe personal injuries and burns to [her] mouth and tongue, as a result of being served extremely hot fries,” according to a civil complaint obtained by The Independent.

In it, Catherine Luongo blames the March 5 incident, which occurred at a McDonald’s restaurant across the street from Manhattan’s Bryant Park, on the employees who “fail[ed] to provide [her] with a safe order of fries.”

Her purported physical trauma was “due solely… [to] the carelessness, recklessness and negligence” of the unnamed workers who prepared the fries in question, which the complaint describes as “overheated and not safe for human consumption.”

Luongo should never have been “permitt[ed] and allow[ed]” to “be served and consume extremely hot and overheated fries,” the complaint states. It contends that Luongo was not given ample warning of “the dangers to be encountered” when tucking into the fries, and that “the aforesaid occurrence was due solely by reason of the negligence of the Defendants,” and “through no fault or lack of care” on Luongo’s part.

On top of Luongo’s alleged mouth and tongue injuries, she also endured “a severe shock to the nervous system,” “suffered great physical pain and mental anguish,” and “was confined to bed and home and caused to abstain from usual duties and activities,” according to the complaint, which was filed July 21 in New York State Supreme Court.

open image in gallery A New York woman is suing McDonald's over injuries she claims she suffered while digging into an order of allegedly superheated fries ( Getty )

It says Luongo was “forced to seek medical aid and attention,” which she had to pay for herself, and claims her fry-related health issues “may be permanent and lasting.” The complaint does not provide further details of Luongo’s alleged injuries.

McDonald’s did not respond to a request for comment.

In 2013, the chain was hauled into court by a Massachusetts mom who sued after her 3-year-old daughter suffered first- and second-degree burns on her thighs from an order of “unreasonably and dangerously hot” fries.

“As a direct and proximate cause of the unreasonably and dangerously hot French Fries, M.C. is now disfigured and scarred,” the lawsuit claimed. “M.C. is undergoing surgery due to the disfigurement and scarring.”

That same year, a Florida woman was awarded $800,000 after her 4-year-old daughter received second-degree burns from a “dangerously hot” Chicken McNugget that fell from its packaging and became wedged between the child’s leg and her seat belt. Philana Holmes used her iPhone to record the girl’s screams, which were played in court.

Lawyers for McDonald’s unsuccessfully argued that the McNugget had to be heated to a certain temperature to stave off the possibility of salmonella poisoning, and, as PBS reported at the time, that the nuggets “were not meant to be pressed between a seat belt and human flesh for more than two minutes.”

A similar suit, this one filed in 2009, involved an order of “dangerously hot” Dunkin’ Donuts hash browns and a Boston-area toddler, who they said received “serious and permanent burn injuries” when the hot potatoes fell from his mouth onto his neck. Before Robin MacLeod gave her son the hash brown, she checked it and found it “lukewarm,” the family’s complaint said.

open image in gallery Catherine Luongo claims she was injured by an order of scaldingly hot fries she purchased at a McDonald's on East 42 Street in Manhattan ( Google Maps )

However, the hash brown had been heated “unevenly,” according to the filing, which claimed the inside of the item was so hot, it was “unsafe for public consumption.”

Beyond the fast-food realm, a Philadelphia man sued Frontier Airlines in 2024 after sustaining third-degree burns and being “left with disfiguring scars on his genitals and thighs” after a flight attendant allegedly spilled hot tea on his lap.

As The Independent first reported, Sean Miller’s complaint detailed the “highly unsightly and embarrassing discoloration,” along with “significantly decreased sensation,” “post-traumatic stress disorder,” and “lack of self-esteem,” plus at least one herniated disc he suffered while writhing in distress.

Upon landing, the 56-year-old was rushed to an area burn center for specialized treatment “due to the severity” of his injuries.

Such lawsuits, including Luongo’s, bring to mind the well-known and widely misunderstood case of 79-year-old Stella Liebeck, who was maligned for bringing a “frivolous” lawsuit over a blisteringly hot cup of McDonald’s coffee, but which turned out to be anything but trivial.

Liebeck suffered horrific third-degree burns across six percent of her body and led to permanent tissue damage after the cup’s superheated contents spilled on her, causing what her physician called one of the worst scalding cases he had ever seen. The New Mexico resident spent a week in the hospital, three weeks recovering at home, and was then hospitalized again to undergo painful debridement and skin grafts.

Liebeck offered to settle for the costs of her medical treatment, about $20,000, and only sued when McDonald’s, which had in fact gotten hundreds of burn complaints before this one, refused to cooperate.

A jury awarded Liebeck $2.7 million in punitive damages for her injuries, which a judge later reduced to $480,000, for what he deemed “willful, wanton, reckless” and “callous” conduct on the part of McDonald's.

Food service establishments have argued that a reasonable adult is aware that certain foods and beverages are hot, and that a potential burn is an “open and obvious” risk they knowingly assume. At the same time, if a product is so hot that normal use could land someone in the hospital, the seller is required to provide an explicit warning to all.

Luongo’s suit says she “has been damaged in a sum which exceeds the jurisdictional limits of all lower Courts,” and is seeking money damages to be determined at trial

The upcoming season of Ted Lasso is introducing brand new characters — but the series’ star and co-creator Jason Sudeikis had to say goodbye to the previous cast first.

Apple TV’s hit series was supposed to end with its 2023 finale as Sudeikis’s titular character returned to the U.S. after three seasons as coach of a British men’s soccer team.

Instead, Sudeikis and his fellow co-creators began to brainstorm about continuing the show. Eventually, they landed on a fourth season centering on an all-female team, the cast and creators told The Hollywood Reporter in an article published Wednesday.

However, the new creative direction meant that the fictional AFC Richmond team at the center of the first seasons would not return. Sudeikis, 50, was tasked with explaining that to the actors who played those teammates in “very difficult” individual phone calls, he told THR.

“Because I didn’t want them to hear it on the internet,” the Saturday Night Live alum told the outlet. “And because I love those guys and we all went through something together.”

open image in gallery Jason Sudeikis will return as Ted Lasso for season four of the Apple TV show ( Getty )

Although the old team will not be coming back to the show, lead actors including Sudeikis, Hannah Waddingham, Jeremy Swift, Juno Temple and Brett Goldstein will all be returning for the long-awaited fourth installment.

Currently, there is no update to whether supporting actors Toheeb Jimoh (Sam), Cristo Fernández (Dani), Kola Bokinni (Isaac) and Billy Harris (Colin) will return, although Jimoh joked that he expected his character to have a funeral in the new episodes. Plus, potential guest appearances still remain on the table.

The Independent has reached out to Apple TV for further comment.

open image in gallery Jason Sudeikis and Hannah Waddingham star as a soccer coach and team owner in ‘Ted Lasso’ ( Apple TV+ )

Phil Dunster, who played Jamie Tartt, will also be absent from season four due to scheduling conflicts with his role in Steve Carell’s comedy Rooster, it was announced earlier this year. The actor told podcaster Zach Sang that leaving the show felt like “the end of school when you graduate.”

In another shake-up, the series recast the child actor who plays Henry, Sudeikis’s character’s son. Grant Feely will take over the role in the new episodes.

An official logline for season four, out August 5, reads: “Ted returns to Richmond, taking on his biggest challenge yet: coaching a second division women’s football team. Throughout the course of the season, Ted and the team learn to leap before they look, taking chances they never thought they would.”

The cyclospora cayetanensis parasite has caused a record 12,000 U.S. cases of the stomach bug cyclosporiasis this year, resulting in nasty symptoms including “explosive diarrhea,” vomiting and body aches.

People fall ill by eating produce or drinking water that is contaminated with the parasite, which lives in human waste.

That means an unsavory chain of events is likely behind the current outbreaks, although the source has not yet been identified by public health officials.

The parasite is often spread through traces of human waste that end up in water used on crops, Dr. David Relman, a professor of medicine at Stanford Medicine, explained earlier this month.

That’s the source of most major outbreaks - and potentially this one, other experts told The New York Times this week.

open image in gallery Water irrigating crops can be a source of cyclospora contamination that leads to big outbreaks ( AFP via Getty Images )

“You’d have to have a lot of produce being irrigated with a lot of water that was contaminated by a lot of cyclospora to see this number of cases,” Keith Schneider, a professor of food safety at the University of Florida, told the paper.

But that’s not the only way cyclospora can spread. When an individual handles contaminated crops - whether during growing, harvesting or processing - the parasite can attach to other crops that haven’t been sprayed with contaminated water.

And if a person infected with cyclosporiasis goes to the bathroom and doesn’t properly wash their hands, that’s another way for the parasite to travel.

“Food can become contaminated when an infected person with poor hand hygiene handles it,” UC Davis Health says.

Humans are the sole reason cyclospora spreads, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. People can only be infected if they swallow the parasite.

open image in gallery This graphic image from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention shows how humans are able to spread cyclospora. The infected food enters the intestines, the parasite replicates inside the body and then it is excreted so it can become infectious again ( CDC )

When cyclospora is swallowed, the parasite infects the small intestine, multiplying in the body’s cells for weeks before it is expelled in feces. After it leaves the body, the parasite needs a couple of weeks to become infectious again in the environment, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment says.

“This time period outside of the body allows the parasite to become infective, which is where it contaminates food or water,” the department wrote.

That’s how the cycle continues.

Unfortunately, it doesn’t take much to become infected and everyone is at risk. Some foods have been more susceptible to cyclospora than others, too. Those include cilantro, raspberries, snow peas, basil and parsley.

“Because leafy greens and berries are usually consumed raw, the parasite can remain viable, even after washing,” Ynes Ortega, a food safety expert at the University of Georgia, pointed out.

Contaminated lettuce has been linked to cases in Great Lakes states and the Midwest, according to the FDA, but the investigation into cases remains ongoing.

While washing produce can help to reduce risk, it doesn’t eliminate the parasite. The only way to kill it is to cook food at 158 degrees Fahrenheit.

That’s part of the problem, too.

“Our fresh produce system is really a web, a network, going out to grocery stores, restaurants and schools. The produce industry and other stakeholders do the best they can to prevent these outbreaks,” Gerardo "Jerry" Lopez, an associate professor at the University of Arizona, said. “But once the parasite is on produce, it's hard to get off.”

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: Arsenal get William Saliba injury update as star ‘makes surgery decision’ following World Cup blow
Sports.content:
ARSENAL fear William Saliba will miss MONTHS of the new season after deciding not to undergo surgery to overcome his back problem.

The defender, 25, was forced off during France’s World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain last week.



And there have been concerns that Saliba is in line to be crocked for the start of Arsenal’s Premier League title defence.

The former Marseille man has been weighing up how to get himself back to full fitness.



L’Equipe report Saliba has chosen not to go under the knife after holding talks with Arsenal’s medical department.

It means the centre-back is facing a lengthy period of treatment and needs to rest before being given the green light to return to training.



Saliba wants to keep tabs on the healing process and see how quickly he progresses instead of having an operation.

There have been suggestions he suffered a back fracture during Arsenal’s loss to Bournemouth in April.

But Saliba was determined to play through the pain barrier to keep his World Cup dreams alive and feature in the final weeks of the Gunners’ push for silverware.

The Emirates Stadium favourite said: “I’ve had some minor niggles for several months.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“I’ve been gritting my teeth because there was the Champions League and the Premier League. But the coaching staff are handling it very well.

“The World Cup comes around only once every four years, so you’ve got to grit your teeth.

“I’m not at 100 per cent, but there are plenty of players who aren’t at 100 per cent either. You can’t make excuses.”

Saliba’s injury has resulted in Arsenal considering a move for free agent John Stones as a short-term fix.

The six-time Premier League title winner, 32, is assessing his options after leaving Manchester City.



But Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is facing competition from Chelsea as the new season edges closer.

Sports.title: Newly single Spain hero Ferran Torres and glam singer, 29, ‘spend World Cup after party flirting and teasing’
Sports.content:
SPAIN’S World Cup hero Ferran Torres was reportedly seen flirting with singer Ana Mena while celebrating the team’s famous triumph.

The Barcelona star, 26, is on a high after netting Spain’s winner to secure a 1-0 victory over Argentina in Sunday’s final.



Torres has become a national treasure in the process and he has been lapping up the team’s celebrations in Madrid.

The winger partied with his team-mates during their open-top bus parade in the Spanish capital that ended in the Plaza de Cibeles.



Spain stars then enjoyed an after party, with Mena also securing an invite after performing on stage.

Torres is a newly-single man after rumours that he broke up with girlfriend Martina Hunter during the World Cup.

Spanish journalist Javi de Hoyos claimed the couple split just before Spain’s 2-1 win over Belgium in the quarter-finals on July 10.

And it seems Torres is moving on quickly after being spotted with Mena during the Spain team’s celebrations.

And Mena’s fellow singer Amor Romeira – who was also at the party – confirmed there was “flirting” between the pair.

She said in a response to a fan on Instagram: “There was flirting, some teasing.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“They were together all night and there was a lot of chemistry. It was like they were on a date.”

Meanwhile, reporter Gerard Romero said the pair had “very good chemistry” together after speaking on Twitch stream.

He also pointed out that Mena was later seen wearing a Spain shirt with the No 7 on it that he believes belongs to Torres.

Romero said on his stream: “Last night, at the party where Ozuna was, where Myke Towers, Lola Índigo, and Ana Mena were… what jersey was Ana Mena wearing, what number was on it?”



“I’ll just say there was very good chemistry.”

Torres – who once played for Man City – is said to have gone through a bitter break-up with Hunter.

The pair both unfollowed each other on Instagram before Hunter jetted off to Bali to get over her heartbreak.



Torres has also dated Sira Martinez, a professional showjumper and influencer who is the daughter of PSG boss Luis Enrique.

The forward played under Enrique at Barcelona while he was in a relationship with Martinez and made a joke about their romance.

Speaking in 2022, Enrique claimed he would immediately sub the player if he ever celebrated with a baby gesture.

He said: “I would replace him in that moment, put him on the stands, and he wouldn’t set foot on a football pitch again.”

Sports.title: Alex Scott ‘picks preferred team’ as Man Utd, Chelsea and Arsenal circle for £80m-rated Bournemouth star
Sports.content:
ALEX SCOTT reportedly wants to seal a mega-money move to Chelsea instead of Manchester United or Arsenal.

The Bournemouth midfielder, 22, put his admirers on red alert after rejecting a new contract at the Vitality Stadium.



And Chelsea tried to tempt the Cherries into selling Scott for £64million, only for the bid to be turned down.

But it appears the former Bristol City man has not given up on completing a dream switch to Stamford Bridge.



The Standard report Scott has pinpointed Chelsea as his preferred destination this summer.

His stance will come as a huge blow for Man Utd and Arsenal, who have shown interest.



The Gunners were already beaten by Chelsea to the £117m signing of Morgan Rogers earlier this week.

And Arsenal supremo Mikel Arteta will be seething if he misses out on another transfer target to Blues chief Xabi Alonso.

But Bournemouth have been desperately attempting to tie Scott down to an improved deal.

New boss Marco Rose, who is preparing for his first season in charge after succeeding Andoni Iraola, sees the talisman as a key part of his plans.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And Bournemouth have attempted to price their sought-after star out of a move by rating him at £80m.

Scott played a pivotal role in the Cherries bagging European qualification for the first time in their history last season.

He made 37 Premier League appearances in the record-breaking campaign, notching three goals and an assist along the way.

That form resulted in Scott being rewarded with the chance to join England’s training camp before the World Cup.



It softened the blow after he was not included in the Three Lions’ 26-man squad for the tournament.

Scott’s step-sister Maya Le Tissier is with Manchester United Women, leading to Old Trafford chiefs hoping she could convince him to head north.

Sports.title: Inter Miami announce signing of former Man Utd star Casemiro but transfer is immediately investigated by MLS
Sports.content:
CASEMIRO has completed a move to Inter Miami – but the switch has landed the MLS side in hot water.

The midfielder, 34, was a free agent after walking away from Manchester United at the end of last season.



And Casemiro, who broke down in tears as he made an emotional farewell speech to Red Devils fans, has penned a one-year deal which has the option of being extended until 2029.

But MLS chiefs have confirmed the transfer is being investigated due to concerns of potentially violating tampering rules.



LA Galaxy held Casemiro’s discovery rights, which led to Inter Miami facing the threat of having to shell out £750,000.

A probe has now been launched to decide whether the Brazilian’s new employers violated regulations to get the deal over the line.

An MLS statement read: “Major League Soccer is reviewing a tampering allegation against Inter Miami CF.

“The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete.

“While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation.”

The size of the fee Inter Miami will pay LA Galaxy for Casemiro’s discovery rights is set to be decided after the investigation.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

The reigning MLS Cup champions were fined more than $2million after being found guilty of ignoring salary cap rules in 2021.

It led to co-owner Jorge Mas being forced to pay $250,000 out of his own pocket and sporting director Paul McDonough was suspended for a year.

But Casemiro, who missed out on World Cup glory after Brazil were knocked out by Norway in the last-16, has not joined Inter Miami as a designated player.

Mas said: “Casemiro’s arrival reflects the vision and ambition that define Inter Miami.



“We never settle. We’re always looking to grow, improve and raise our standards every season.

“We’ve built a global club with the vision of becoming not only the best club in the United States, but also a benchmark globally.”

Casemiro, who made 34 Premier League appearances for United last season, will now have Lionel Messi among his team-mates.

The Real Madrid legend won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup during his time at Old Trafford.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho becomes third Man Utd flop to join Aston Villa in three years and completes medical for Chelsea loan
Sports.content:
ALEJANDRO GARNACHO is closing in on a loan move to Aston Villa after completing a medical.

The winger is set to become the third Red Devils flop to join the club in three years after falling out of favour at Chelsea.



He only signed for the Blues last summer after falling out with old boss Ruben Amorim at Old Trafford.

Garnacho follows Jadon Sancho and Marcus Rashford in trying his luck at Villa Park after a lack of game time.



Rashford had relative success at Villa during his loan spell in 2024-25 as he scored twice and assisted four in the second half of the campaign.

Sancho effectively replaced Rashford the following season after he flopped on loan at Chelsea the previous year.



But the move didn’t go as well for the ex-Borussia Dortmund star as he managed just one goal and three assists across the whole season.

Garnacho will hope to fare better under Unai Emery, who has reportedly been chasing the player since before he joined Chelsea, according to the Athletic.

Villa have agreed a loan deal with a conditional obligation to buy as they look to replace Morgan Rogers – who has headed the other way in a £117m British record deal.

And a four-year contract is in place should the buy option be executed next summer.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He will become the fourth player to arrive at Villa Park this summer after Johan Manzambi, Joao Gomes and Modou Keba Cisse.

The transaction is a tricky one for Villa after selling Rogers to Chelsea for a record price.

UEFA’s rules mean that any permanent signing from Chelsea would count as a “player exchange transaction”.

That means the profit from the Rogers deal would be reduced based on the difference in fees between him and Garnacho.



UEFA’s period for players exchanges covers a 45-day period and there are only 41 days left in the transfer window.

So Villa’s workaround is to agree a conditional loan move that be made permanent next summer.

That also works for Chelsea, who will be able to retain more profit on the Garnacho deal.

Villa are looking to avoid more trouble with Uefa after being fined £19.4million for a “significant breach” of its squad cost rules.

Sports.title: Arsenal’s pre-season plans revealed with 14 players on post-World Cup holidays, Marbella camp and old-school friendlies
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have officially started pre-season this week as they get ready to defend their Premier League crown.

The Gunners lifted the title for the first time in 22 years last season and are determined to retain it.

Mikel Arteta has worked with staff to put together a plan that will get his players up to speed for the new campaign.



Arsenal begin their defence of the Prem on August 21, when they host Coventry City, and want to hit the ground running.



Who is already in training?

Arsenal had 15 players at the World Cup this summer, which means not many of last season’s squad are training right now.

Ben White, who injured his knee in May, is one of them and he is back in full training.

Jurrien Timber is stepping up his rehab after a minor operation last month and hopes to play some part in pre-season.



Those not at the World Cup and now in training include the likes of Christian Norgaard, Cristhian Mosquera, Gabriel Jesus, Myles Lewis-Skelly and Riccardo Calafiori.

Ethan Nwaneri, Fabio Vieira and Reiss Nelson have also reported for duty after being on loan last season.

New signing Illan Meslier has also got to work and is training alongside fellow goalkeepers Kepa Arrizabalaga and Tommy Setford.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Teenage stars Marli Salmon and Max Dowman are with the first team, too, and could get plenty of minutes in pre-season.



When are the World Cup stars back?

Fifa rules state that players are entitled to a minimum of three weeks off during the summer break.

Arsenal had 15 players over in North America this summer and they will return at different times, depending on when they exited the World Cup.

One of those – Leandro Trossard – has already left after joining Besiktas for around £17million earlier this month.

Eight of Arsenal’s squad made it to the final weekend of the World Cup and therefore will not be due back to training until August 10 at the earliest.

That group includes England quartet Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke.



Spain trio David Raya, Martin Zubimendi and Mikel Merino are also part of it, as is France’s William Saliba.

There is a chance they are given more than three weeks off, with Arsenal’s first Prem game not until August 21, and players’ return dates will be decided on a case-by-case basis.

Arsenal’s six other players at the World Cup this summer were Gabriel Magalhaes, Gabriel Martinelli, Kai Havertz, Martin Odegaard, Piero Hincapie and Viktor Gyokeres.

The two Gabriels, Havertz, Hincapie and Gyokeres all went out before the quarter-finals of the World Cup – and so should return to training next week.

Odegaard and Norway made it to the last 8 and so a three-week break for him would see the Gunners skipper back in early August.



What do Arsenal have planned?

Arsenal officially started pre-season on Monday, although they held a mini training camp in Marbella last week.

Arteta has organised a similar event in the past and did so again this year, inviting players to bring their families along, too.

Arsenal have kept their pre-season plans low key this summer after a gruelling season that was 63 games long.

They have also started later than other sides due to having 15 players at the World Cup and last season not finishing until May 30.

They are not going on a farflung tour across the globe and instead will head to Spain later this month for a proper training camp.



That will coincide with the Gunners having their first friendly of the summer at Girona on August 1.

Four days later, they will take on Real Betis in Dublin before flying back to London for two friendlies at the Emirates.

They are taking on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup on August 9 and then host Como three days later.

All of that is designed to get Arsenal ready and firing for the Community Shield with Manchester City in Cardiff on August 16.

What new faces are there and will more be coming?

Arsenal have made Hincapie’s loan move from Bayer Leverkusen permanent for £34.5million and signed Meslier on a free transfer after his contract with Leeds expired.



Christos Tzolis is undergoing a medical this week and will join from Club Brugge for a fee of £34m.

The winger has already played friendlies for Brugge this summer and so is ready to get work with Arsenal.

The club are working on more signings and still want to add a defender, midfielder and forward.

There have been changes to the medical department over the summer and the new staff are running sessions this week.

The new hires include Arnaldo Abrantes joining from Aston Villa as club doctor.



Eneko Angulo arrives from Real Betis as a rehabilitation specialist and Bayer Leverkusen fitness coach Jose Jimenez has been added to the ranks as well.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They have come in after club doctor Zafar Iqbal and head of sports science and performance Tom Allen both left.

Sam Wilson, lead physical performance coach, has also departed after being poached by Italian side Parma.

Sports.title: As Morgan Rogers calls Chelsea ‘biggest team in London’ SunSport argue whether Blues or Arsenal are really capital kings
Sports.content:
MORGAN ROGERS completed his record £117million transfer to Chelsea and immediately said he had joined the “biggest club in London”.

That’s no small claim, given rivals Arsenal won the league in May while the Blues finished down in tenth.



The Gunners have enjoyed the best of the recent seasons, but Chelsea have had more than their share of the successes in the past 20 years.

So which club is REALLY the “biggest in London”?



SunSport’s Arsenal reporter (and Gooner) Simon Collings has gone toe-to-toe with SunSport’s Chelsea reporter (and diehard Blue) Lloyd Canfield to argue their case…

ARSENAL

By Simon Collings



Morgan Rogers has ruffled a few feathers with the suggestion that he’s joined the biggest club in London.

But as you can tell from what’s behind me I’m going to have to respectfully disagree with him.



The easiest thing for me to make my argument as to why Arsenal right now are the biggest club in London… just take a look at the Premier League table from last season.

Take a look at who are the champions. Yes, that’s right. It’s Arsenal.

Rodgers can talk all about joining the biggest club in London, but the fact is he’s joined a side that finished 10th last season.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

And Chelsea fans, well, they might like to point towards history and European Cups and trophies, but there’s only one team that’s gone a whole Premier League season unbeaten and that is Arsenal.

CHELSEA

By Lloyd Canfield

So a shock… my colleague Simon Collings and a bunch of Arsenal fans seem to think that Morgan Rogers is wrong and Chelsea are not the biggest club in London.



Well, I know for a fact it’s not Arsenal. It’s not no ‘European Trophies Arsenal’. I know that’s right.

How about put your European trophies on the table? Yeah, put your world champions trophies on the table. How about that?

But Chelsea have got so much history in class and so many Premier League trophies and FA Cups…



Get a grip. You should be arguing with Spurs. You shouldn’t be arguing with me.

You should be arguing with Tom Barclay our Spurs reporter because they’ve got more European trophies than you.

We’ve got more European trophies than you. West Ham have got more European trophies than you…

You can’t even say ‘well, we haven’t won them because we’re not in the Europa League.’ When you were in the Europa League you bottled it to us.

Even though Arsenal won the Premier League they’re not signing the calibre of players that Premier League champions who are going to go on and do it again are signing.



Chelsea took Morgan Rogers. Spurs have got Sandro Tonali. They nearly got relegated. Every other team seems to be having a better window than Arsenal.

If you’re going to claim you’re the biggest club in London, you better step up and start acting like it because right now that’s not what I’m seeing.

Let’s talk next season. I know Chelsea finished 10th. I’m aware of that. But this isn’t based on one season.

Don’t start acting up after one good season where you won the league because we’ve been there we’ve done that.



Realistically, the only argument Arsenal could make is maybe having more global fans or maybe more fans in London.

But either way if we’re talking about global fan base in the modern day, Arsenal have got 11 million fewer Instagram followers than Chelsea.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

To give you some credit, 25 years ago you almost definitely would have won that argument, but now we’re not living in those times anymore.

Times have changed. Chelsea are, in fact, the biggest club in London, so… sorry, Simon.

Sports.title: Rangers boss Derek McInnes discovers SFA punishment as he learns if he’ll be BANNED for first Gers game in charge
Sports.content:
DEREK McINNES will be BANNED from the touchline for his first competitive game as Rangers manager – and FURTHER games after it.

That’s after the SFA ruled over his comments in the wake of the controversial penalty decision in the Motherwell v Celtic match at the end of last season.



McInnes, 55, was appointed Rangers boss last month, making a stunning move from Hearts.

He made the switch having led the Jambos to a title charge last season with their bid to be champions ended in devastating fashion by Celtic on the final day of the season.



But while two months have now passed since the Premiership season ended, the impact of the dramatic finish to the campaign is still being felt.

Last month, McInnes was hit with a notice of complaint by the SFA.

And now, he’s been slapped with a FOUR-match ban by Hampden chiefs.

Three will be served immediately with the fourth game suspended until the end of the season.

McInnes was charged in relation to comments made in the aftermath of a highly controversial penultimate round of fixtures.

Hearts beat Falkirk on the night in question but it was what McInnes had to say regarding Celtic’s win at Motherwell that landed him in hat water.



OUR BEST FREE BETS & SIGN-UP OFFERS

That game was settled by a Kelechi Iheanacho penalty with THE last kick of the game, securing the Hoops a vital 3-2 win in the title race.

McInnes branded the decision to award Celtic a penalty as “disgusting.”

The controversial decision saw referee John Beaton point to the spot after VAR review, with Sam Nicholson ruled to have handled the ball in an aerial challenge with Auston Trusty.

Speaking to Sky Sports, he said: “When you heard Celtic got a 96th minute penalty that was going to VAR and they were checking it, you just assume what’s happened is they get the penalty.

“Having seen it again, it’s disgusting. It is.



“I don’t think it’s a penalty kick. But we’re up against it. We’re up against everybody.”

Hampden chiefs deemed McInnes had broken rule 72 of the SFA disciplinary guidelines.

The full notice of complaint reads: The notice for McInnes reads: “Disciplinary Rule 72 – No recognised football body, club, official, Team Official or other member of Team Staff, player or other person under the jurisdiction of the Scottish FA, shall in an interview, a ‘blog’ on the internet, on a social networking or micro-blogging site, or in any other manner calculated or likely to lead to publicity (i) criticise the Decision(s) and/or performance(s) of any or all match official(s) in such a way as to indicate bias or incompetence on the part of such match official; or (ii) make remarks about such match official(s) which impinge on his character.

“For the avoidance of doubt this Rule applies (i) whether reported to the Scottish FA by a match official for Misconduct or otherwise, and (ii) where remarks are brought to the Scottish FA’s attention, or of which the Scottish FA becomes aware, by whatever manner or means.

“There shall be a resumption that any material published in such manner was published in the name of and/or with the authority of the person or body bearing to have published the material.”



Now, at a hearing, McInnes has discovered his fate.

SunSport exclusively revealed prior to the hearing that McInnes was making a personal appearance with the understanding being the Gers boss wanted to speak up on his own behalf at the showdown.

We revealed how a key part of McInnes’ defence was to feature similar comments made by ex-Celtic star Peter Grant, who when employed as Alloa manager in 2021 labelled a decision ‘disgusting’ and wasn’t subject to any disciplinary action.

And as mentioned, the SFA’s decision is that McInnes has been given a four-game ban – with THREE to be served immediately and one suspended until the end of the season.



That means McInnes will be forced into the stands for his first game in charge against Dundee United on July 31 as well as the following two matches.

He will therefore be absent from the dugout for Rangers’ clash with Hibs on August 9 and the Gers’ first Premier Sports Cup match of the season the following weekend.

That means McInnes’ first domestic game on the touchline will be at Ibrox against St Mirren on Sunday, August 22.

Of course, the suspension won’t have any effect on his availability for European matches.



Therefore, McInnes is free to coach from the touchline for Rangers’ double-header against Jagiellonia Bialystok in Europa League qualifying on August 6 and August 13.

The decision on the SFA disciplinary website reads: “Proved. Four match suspension applied as follows: three matches immediate and one match suspended until the end of season 2026/27, suspended sanction applicable only should Derek McInnes further breach Disciplinary Rule 72 within this period.”

Motherwell star Elliot Watt and the Fir Park club themselves had also been hit with a charge in relation to the post-match fall out from game against Celtic.

The midfielder was slapped with a FOUR-game ban, with the club fined £5,000.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

However, Watt will NOT serve the ban after completing a transfer to Turkish club Samsunspor in the days that followed.

Sports.title: Sky Sports host, 41, wrongly diagnosed with cancer AGAIN as she describes 'emotional toll'
Sports.content:
Sky Sports host, 41, wrongly diagnosed with cancer AGAIN as she describes 'emotional toll'

Jo Wilson endured the traumatic experience of being told her cancer had returned this year, despite the Sky Sports News presenter having been given the all clear years earlier

View Image Jo Wilson is aiming to raise awareness after receiving an incorrect cancer diagnosis

Sky Sports News presenter Jo Wilson has opened up about the emotional impact it has had on her upon receiving a second, incorrect cancer diagnosis, just three years after being declared all clear following her year‑long battle with stage three cervical cancer. The 41-year-old has documented her journey with the disease.

‌



She was first diagnosed in June 2022 after a routine smear test, which led to her undergoing life‑saving radiotherapy and chemotherapy treatment. Wilson produced a documentary highlighting football figures who had also faced cancer battles titled 'Football, Cancer and Me,' which was released in November 2025.

‌



On Tuesday, Wilson took to Instagram to raise awareness after being told this year that her cancer had returned. In a touching post where she shared several photos from the hospital, she wrote: "A little life update, please read until the end (red heart emoji).

‌



Man Utd and Arsenal locked in £40million transfer battle as duo hold talks over deal READ MORE :

5 attackers Arsenal could still sign after Morgan Rogers transfer setback READ MORE :

"In February, after my three-year scan, I was told my cancer had returned in a lymph node. I couldn't believe it - it felt like my whole world had crumbled all over again. But after being referred to the high-dose radiotherapy team, one consultant questioned whether the diagnosis was actually correct.

"What followed were five months of tests, scans, waiting and uncertainty before, last week, I finally got the news I’d been desperately hoping for: it wasn’t cancer after all. The lymph node is now thought to be a benign neuroma - a cluster of nerves that was likely inflamed at the time of my original scan. The relief was indescribable, but so too is the emotional toll from the last five months, believing - then not knowing if my cancer had returned.

"Living with that uncertainty was incredibly hard. On the outside, life carried on - I worked, was being a mum, played (lots of) padel, spent time with friends and family, and smiled for photos. But underneath it all, I was carrying something very heavy, and there were times I found myself in some very dark places.

‌



"So why am I sharing this? Firstly, because we often talk about being 'cancer free', but I'm not sure any of us ever truly feel free of it. The fear of recurrence can stay with you long after treatment ends, and I think it’s important we talk about that reality. If you’re someone living beyond a cancer diagnosis, please know you’re not alone."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

The presenter continued: "Secondly, because social media is never the full picture. The last few months on here have probably looked like lots of happy moments, lovely places and time with people I love - and those moments were all real. But they existed alongside this. Instagram is a highlight reel, not the whole story.

‌



"And finally, because we never really know what someone else is carrying. A friend, a colleague, the person serving you coffee or standing next to you in the supermarket - they could be fighting a battle you know nothing about. So this is simply a reminder to be kind. Always (red heart emoji). Thank you to my incredible support network, you know who you are."

In her documentary, Wilson revealed that the diagnosis had changed her life 'in an instant', coming just shortly after the birth of her daughter Mabel.

"It hit me like a truck," she said. "I did wonder if I'm going to die. I'd prepared myself for the worst, I think you have to.

‌



"I actually didn't tell anyone. I didn't want to put it on anyone. If one person can see this and make a phone call to the doctor because something doesn't feel right, then it's worth talking about."

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

She underwent daily radiotherapy, weekly chemotherapy and three days of invasive internal brachytherapy across a five‑week period. It meant being separated from her daughter, a period she described as the 'darkest' phase of her illness.

‌



The broadcaster, who joined Sky Sports in 2011, has urged women to book their cervical smear test in light of her own cancer diagnosis. Around one in 130 women in the UK will be diagnosed with cervical cancer in their lifetime, yet one in three do not attend their smear test.

"I must raise awareness," she previously said. "I want people to talk about what’s stopping them from going to their tests.

"Is it finding time? Is it embarrassment? Whatever support you need, or why you ever haven’t gone for a smear - go and be tested. I promise you, it’s far better than going through cancer."
