Sports.title: Southampton head coach Tonda Eckert charged with misconduct by FA over spygate scandal
Sports.content:
Southampton’s manager, Tonda Eckert, is facing a lengthy suspension from all football activity after being charged with three counts of misconduct by the Football Association.

They relate to the Spygate scandal and involve breaching FA rules during covert missions to illicitly observe Championship training sessions involving Middlesbrough, Ipswich and Oxford last season.

The 33-year-old has until Tuesday to respond to the charges and may well fear the precedent set by Fifa when it banned Bev Priestman, the English-born former Canada women’s head coach and assistant England women coach, from football worldwide for 12 months.

In 2024 Priestman, then in charge of Canada, was found to have authorised the use of a drone to monitor New Zealand’s training during the Paris Olympics.

Southampton have already been punished for Spygate by the English Football League when in May an independent disciplinary commission found the Championship club guilty of three counts of football espionage.

That ruling stripped Eckert’s team of their right to appear in the playoff final in addition to ruling that they must start the coming Championship campaign handicapped by a four-point deduction. The EFL, though, has no power to issue sanctions against individuals in such instances, so the case against Eckert was handed to the FA, which launched a long-running inquiry.

At the start of July the governing body spoke to Eckert, a former analyst for the Germany national team, at length and have the power to issue a range of punishments, ranging from a warning to a heavy fine to suspension.

Yet whereas Priestman’s ban was worldwide, the FA only possess the power to prevent Eckert working in England. The governing body does, however, have the right to ask Fifa to apply any suspension internationally.

View image in fullscreen Tonda Eckert takes charge of a pre-season friendly for Southampton. Photograph: James Marsh/Shutterstock

In 2023, the Italian FA succeeded with such a request when they demanded that the then Newcastle midfielder Sandro Tonali’s 10-month suspension for betting irregularities be applied worldwide. In Eckert’s case, an England-only ban would appear almost meaningless were he to be offered a job abroad.

Eckert has already apologised to Southampton fans and admitted he should have known that EFL regulations specifically outlawed spying. A coach who grew up within a European culture that tacitly tolerates observing rivals’ training sessions also spoke of the “bitter irony” that Southampton’s three spying missions had “no impact” on his team’s planning or performances.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

William Salt, the intern first-team analyst, was caught filming Middlesbrough’s training session on a mobile phone before the first leg of a playoff semi-final won on aggregate by Southampton before their expulsion. He has since been offered a permanent post in the club’s academy. Salt has not been the subject of any FA charges.

Southampton’s owner, Dragan Solak, has vowed to stand by Eckert and has maintained he will not sack him. But a possible 12-month – or, as some sources are suggesting, six-month FA ban – could alter that stance.

In a statement on Wednesday Southampton said: “Tonda and the club will continue to cooperate fully and openly with the FA. Our focus remains on preparations for the 2026-27 season. The club remains fully supportive of Tonda and his staff as we work towards our ambition of returning to the Premier League.”

Eckert, who saw Middlesbrough take Southampton’s place in a playoff final won by Hull, recently told BBC Radio Solent: “I’ve held my hand up for this judgment on something I have authorised. I am responsible and I apologise for bad judgment.”

Back in 2019, the FA issued formal warnings to the then Leeds manager Marcelo Bielsa and a club analyst for spying on Derby, but English football’s regulations have since been tightened.

Sports.title: ‘A unique talent’: Phil Foden signs new four-year Manchester City contract
Sports.content:
Phil Foden has signed a new four-year contract with Manchester City, saying he is looking forward to “trying to win more” at his boyhood club. The deal, which has an additional 12-month option, ties the 26-year-old to the club until 2030.

Foden is relishing working again with Enzo Maresca. The new City manager was Pep Guardiola’s ­assistant during the 2022-23 treble-winning season.

Foden said: “Committing my future to City means everything to me. Playing for this club is all I’ve ever wanted to do and it’s always an honour to wear the shirt. It’s not lost on me that I’ve been lucky enough to be part of a historic period with so many titles won, but we’re always looking to the future and trying to win more.

“I can only thank the club, staff, teammates and fans who continue to put their faith in me. I hope I’ll be able to repay you for years to come. I can’t wait to work with Enzo again. He was brilliant during the treble season – someone all the players respected and loved working with.

“To have him back here is exciting. Personally, I know I’ve improved so much from ­working with our coaches and world-class squad. I am excited for the next phase of my career at this great club.”

With John Stones and Bernardo Silva having left the club, Foden is City’s most decorated player with 17 major honours. The forward has won six Premier Leagues, one Champions League, three FA Cups, five League Cups, one Uefa Super Cup and one Club World Cup.

Foden expressed disbelief at how long he has been at City. “Not in a million years [would I think this],” he said. “I would say I had a dream to make it to the first team, but to stay this long, it’s a dream. And like I said, I’m just enjoying it and trying to make the most of it.”

Foden is hopeful Maresca’s mode of play will suit him. “You can tell by the first few sessions I’ve done with him – the way he likes to play out from the back and play a lot of possession-based – it suits my game really well. I’m looking forward to that and hopefully it can help my game go to the next stage,” he said.

The new deal indicates the firm belief of Maresca and Hugo Viana, the director of football, that Foden can recapture his form. He lost his starting place under Guardiola and was left out of England’s World Cup squad. Foden’s form has fallen away since he was a key part of City’s 2023-24 title success and winning the Football Writers’ Association and Professional Footballers’ Association player of the year awards.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Phil Foden says he is hoping his game can reach another level with Enzo Maresca. Photograph: Manchester City

Last season, after the 2-2 draw with Nottingham Forest on 4 March, Foden started two league games and was substituted after 58 minutes of the 2-1 FA Cup final victory over Southampton. Foden has spent his whole career with City, joining as an eight-year-old.

Viana said: “Everyone at ­Manchester City is incredibly proud of Phil. He represents everything good about our academy. He is a unique ­talent and his creativity is a joy to watch. None of what he has achieved would be possible without the focus, dedication and humility to work hard in every moment and absorb all of the knowledge available to him through our coaches and players.

“At 26, his development is still ongoing, and we look forward to ­seeing the player Phil can become over the coming years.”

After the 2025 FA Cup 1-0 final defeat by Crystal Palace, Foden revealed he had been struggling with off-field problems. He had also played with pain after suffering an ankle problem sustained from a Casemiro tackle in a goalless draw at ­Manchester United in April.

Sports.title: Ipswich Town finalising move for Celtic and World Cup star in £10m deal
Sports.content:
Ipswich Town finalising move for Celtic and World Cup star in £10m deal

Ipswich Town are formalising a move for Celtic forward Daizen Maeda, talkSPORT understands.

The total package is set to be worth £10million.

2 Maeda has proved tremendous value for money with Celtic Credit: Getty

Maeda would join Ipswich following a trophy-laden four-and-a-half years at Celtic Park.

Since his arrival in December 2021, the 28-year-old has won ten pieces of silverware.

Of those ten, five were Celtic's Scottish Premiership triumphs, along with three Scottish Cups and two Scottish League Cups.

On an individual basis, Maeda produced his best displays in the 2024/25 campaign as he bagged 33 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions.

His brilliance that season was recognised by being named the PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year, Celtic Player of the Year and an inclusion in the PFA Scotland Team of the Year.

In total, Maeda has scored 79 goals for the Hoops from 212 appearances.

Maeda is also fresh off four appearances for Japan at the World Cup.

The forward started three of Japan's four matches, contributing one assist.

Ipswich's hectic summer

Maeda's mooted arrival continues what has been a busy summer for the Tractor Boys following their promotion from the Championship.

Ipswich will go into the new campaign with a new manager for the first time since December 2021 after Kieran McKenna chose to step down.

2 O'Neil is desperate to avoid an instant return to the Championship with Ipswich Credit: AFP

He was swiftly replaced by Gary O'Neil, who was plucked from Ligue 1 side Strasbourg.

Following O'Neil's arrival, Ipswich have brought in a string of players, including striker Emersonn from Toulouse for a club-record £26.6million.

Leicester City forward Abdul Fawatu is another key addition, as is Moroccan centre-back Issa Diop from Fulham.

Cedric Kipre and Chuba Akpom also returned to Ipswich on a permanent basis after a successful loan spell last term.

Ipswich begin their Premier League campaign on August 22 against Sunderland.

Sports.title: Leicester explore sale of club ten years after 5000/1 Premier League win
Sports.content:
Leicester's owners are reportedly exploring the sale of the club, a decade on from their Premier League title success.

According to the Financial Times, the Foxes' King Power owners have brought in investment bankers at Citigroup to help sound out potential buyers.

3 Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman in 2018 Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, Sky Sports news report that an unnamed Middle Eastern firm are interested in buying the club, whose portfolio has been shown to a number of potential investors by their advisors.

Should a change in ownership materialise, this would bring an end to one of football's most remarkable ownership stories.

End of an era?

King Power's billionaire founder, Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha, took over at Leicester in 2010, with the team mid-table in the Championship.

In 2014, they won promotion to the Premier League, before enjoying arguably the game's greatest fairy tale story two years later.

Under Claudio Ranieri, the Foxes pulled off one of the greatest shocks in sporting history as they lifted the league title.

The club enjoyed continued success in the years that followed, reaching the quarter-finals of the Champions League in 2017.

But tragedy struck in 2018 when Srivaddhanaprabha died in a helicopter crash outside the team’s stadium, with his son Aiyawatt - known as Top - subsequently taking control of the club.

While Leicester tasted FA Cup glory in 2021, things have taken a turn for the worse at the King Power Stadium since then.

The Foxes suffered relegation from the Premier League in 2023, before bouncing back the following season under Enzo Maresca.

Their return didn't last long though, and they were relegated again in 2025, before disaster struck in the recently-concluded 2025/26 campaign.

3 The football world fell in love with Leicester after their most improbable title success Credit: AFP or licensors

A decade on from their 5000/1 Premier League title success, the East Midlands outfit finished second-bottom in the Championship, condemning them to League One.

Financial woes

Their relegation came amid a backdrop of ongoing financial issues behind the scenes.

Leicester were deducted six points in February after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules for the 2023/24 season.

They breached the EFL Profit and Sustainability Rules (P&S Rules) by reporting losses of £201.9million in the three-year period between 2022 and 2024.

Accounts released this year showed the club lost £71.1million during the 2024/25 Premier League campaign.

In 2025, Leicester's owners wiped £124m of shareholder loans to the club, which converted the debt to equity.

Unsurprisingly, the Foxes' continued financial woes off the pitch and struggles on it has led to chairman Srivaddhanaprabha facing huge criticism from fans, after years of questionable decisions.

3 The King Power ownership is plain to see at Leicester, with their stadium bearing its name Credit: Getty

The current ownership has relocated the club into a multi-million-pound training ground in Seagrave and had explored expanding the current stadium capacity to 40,000.

However, plans for the latter have been put on hold following relegation, with the ground set to remain in its 32,000-seater form.

King Power’s core business has been hit by a drop in visitors to Thailand in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic, especially from China.

Airports of Thailand said in October it had agreed to renegotiate some of the company’s retail concession contracts.

Sports.title: New Rangers boss Derek McInnes to miss first three games in dugout as he’s slapped with ban
Sports.content:
New Rangers boss Derek McInnes to miss first three games in dugout as he’s slapped with ban

New Rangers boss Derek McInnes has copped a three-match touchline ban following comments he made about Scottish officials.

McInnes was hit with a four-game ban, with one suspended, for criticising the decision to award Celtic a late penalty against Motherwell towards the end of last season.



2 McInnes was left seething after Celtic were given a controversial penalty Credit: Getty

The new 'Gers boss was in charge of Hearts at the time, who were locked in a tussle for the Scottish Premiership title with Celtic but ultimately fell short.

Against Motherwell, Celtic were awarded a penalty in the ninth minute of second-half stoppage time for a contentious handball, which they ultimately converted to win the game.

What did McInnes say to land him in hot water?

McInnes labelled referee John Beaton's decision to point to spot, following a recommendation from video assistant Andrew Dallas, as 'quite disgusting.'



"I shouldn't be commenting on another game, but having seen that, it feels like us against everybody," McInnes added.

Had Celtic not beaten Motherwell, Hearts would have won their first Scottish Premiership in 66 years.



Instead, the Hoops' win over Motherwell had them just one point behind Hearts going into the final day.

As it transpired, Celtic broke Hearts' spirits when Daizen Maeda gave them a 2-1 lead in the 87th minute before Callum Osmand put the cherry on top in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to spark a chaotic pitch invasion.



The devastating manner of defeat had Hearts players in tears upon their return from Celtic Park.

Following Hearts' devastating end to the season, McInnes joined Rangers after predecessor Danny Rohl moved to RB Salzburg.

McInnes' switch to Rangers reunited him with striker Lawrence Shankland, who had joined the Scottish giants from Hearts only weeks earlier.

2 McInnes twisted the knife further into Hearts as he followed Shankland to Ibrox Credit: Getty



Which Rangers games will McInnes miss?

The ban means McInnes will be absent from Rangers' Scottish Premiership season opener away to Dundee United on July 31.

He will also miss Hibernian's visit to Ibrox on August 9 and Rangers' second round clash in the Scottish League Cup against a yet-to-be-named opponent over the weekend of August 15-16.

However, McInnes will be available to take charge of Rangers' Europa League qualifiers against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok.

McInnes' side will make the trip to Poland for the first leg of their third qualifying round tie on August 6 before contesting the second leg at Ibrox on August 13.



The 55-year-old's first competitive match as Rangers boss in a Scottish competition falls on August 22 against St Mirren.

Sports.title: Man City confident of reaching deal for World Cup sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi
Sports.content:
Manchester City are increasingly hopeful of signing Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, talkSPORT understands.

Bouaddi, who was a breakout star for Morocco at the World Cup, has been a target for multiple Premier League giants this summer.

4 City are confident they can complete the signing of Bouaddi this summer Credit: Getty

The teenage sensation had previously held talks with Arsenal and Liverpool, while Chelsea were among those tracking him.

However, it's Man City who believe they are close to a deal, with Lille understood to be wanting £85.3million for their star.

And it is believed that City will not to be loaning Bouaddi back to the Ligue 1 side to continue his development.

This comes after Lille made it clear that they preferred to delay a transfer of the 18-year-old by a year.

Good to Bouadd

The French side are prepared to sell him, but have been offering a discounted deal if clubs were open to a loan back or pre-agreement.

If City were to let Bouaddi stay with his current team for another year, they could get a deal done for £68.2m instead.

But that doesn't seem like the case, with Enzo Maresca and co. wanting the midfielder to join straight away and be part of the squad.

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs revealed on July 1: "This is a fascinating transfer story because Lille are prepared to sell, but they heavily favour a deal for 2027, clubs, and Manchester City, have shown they are willing to at least discuss this."

"It's €80m [£68.2m] at the moment, but could come down for those that say to Lille a loan back or pre-agreement," he added.

"It's €100m [£85.3m] for other clubs that want an immediate transfer, so that's going to be one to watch."

4 Bouaddi starred for Morocco at the World Cup and dominated against Brazil in the 1-1 draw Credit: Getty

4 The teenagers started in five matches in North America

Bouaddi's brilliant summer

Man City are set to move for Bouaddi following his incredible World Cup campaign, which saw him catch the eye.

He started every game but one for Morocco at the tournament in North America.

His performance against Brazil instantly had fans in awe, as he stood out against the South American giants.

Bouaddi had the most touches (88), won the most duels (11) and completed the most successful passes in the opposition’s half (30).

His 60 completed passes also made him the second youngest player to complete over 50 passes in a World Cup match in 60 years.

And he would go on to impress again against Scotland, the Netherlands and Canada before struggling against France.

4 Bouaddi could end up being Man City's next midfield arrival after Anderson Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

But Bouaddi remains one of the most sought-after midfielders on the planet, with City hoping to get a deal over the line.

Maresca, who is set for his first campaign in charge, is looking to bolster his midfield after losing Bernardo Silva.

He has already secured the £116m signing of Elliot Anderson, but Bouaddi may also join the talented ranks.

City have signed Anderson, Jeremy Monga, Pierce Charles and Mathys Detourbet so far this summer.

Sports.title: Axel Disasi offered Chelsea escape route as two European clubs express interest
Sports.content:
Chelsea centre-back Axel Disasi is attracting interest from AC Milan and Roma, talkSPORT understands.

The 28-year-old is not in the Blues' plans going forward following the arrival of new boss Xabi Alonso.



2 Disasi's three-year stay at Chelsea could be coming to an end this summer Credit: Getty

Disasi has not reported back for Chelsea pre-season training as both he and the club look for him to find a new team.

Valued at around £25million by the west London outfit, Chelsea stand to make a loss on him.

Signed from Monaco in 2023 for £38m, the defender has failed to hold down a regular starting spot at Stamford Bridge.



Having featured in 44 games in his opening season - scoring on his debut in a 1-1 draw with Liverpool - he quickly soon fell out of favour.

The five-cap France international was shipped off on loan to Aston Villa for the second half of the 2024/25 term - appearing in seven Premier League games.



And having failed to feature for Chelsea in the first half of last season, he then joined West Ham on loan.

Disasi quickly endeared himself to the Hammers faithful as he slotted in alongside Konstantinos Mavropanos in the heart of the back four.



While he scored once from 17 games across all competitions, he ultimately failed to help West Ham remain in the top-flight.

Axel to grind

talkSPORT understands that the east London side had wanted to bring Disasi back to the London Stadium.

However, the player has no desire in competing in the Championship - opening the door to a potential move to Italy.

2 Disasi impressed for West Ham from his 14 Premier League outings



Both Roma and Milan are willing to offer Disasi an escape route from his Chelsea nightmare.

Roma can offer the ex-Reims star Champions League football, where he would reunite with former Villa teammate Donyell Malen.

Meanwhile, Milan will be plying their trade in the Europa League.

The Rossoneri have made it a habit in recent years to raid Chelsea for players in either permanent transfers or loan deals.

Christian Pulisic, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Olivier Giroud, Tiemoue Bakayoko, Joao Felix and Christopher Nkunku have all made the direct switch since 2021.



Should Disasi be sold, Chelsea could look to replace him with another French centre-back in Crystal Palace's Maxence Lacroix.

Sports.title: Why Alejandro Garnacho could trump Marcus Rashford as Unai Emery’s best Aston Villa resurrection act yet
Sports.content:
Why Alejandro Garnacho could trump Marcus Rashford as Unai Emery’s best Aston Villa resurrection act yet

It's become a common theme of Unai Emery's tenure at Aston Villa.

In the last two seasons, the Spaniard has become enamoured with a player who, for whatever reason, has lost their way.

6 Emery has worked with a number of high-profile stars over the years Credit: Getty

Let's rewind to the summer of 2024, when Villa were preparing for their maiden Champions League campaign following the competition's re-brand in 1991.

One Fel swoop

Joao Felix, who had joined Atletico Madrid from Benfica in an eye-watering £113million deal five years earlier, was high in Emery's thinking.

But Villa were not targeting the same Felix that convinced Atleti to fork out a nine-figure sum.

As talented as Felix may have been, there were questions over his consistency and effort.

"He (Felix) has all the qualities to be an incredible player, but as good as you are, if you don't work, it's not enough," Saul Niguez, Felix's former teammate at Atleti, previously said on Spanish radio.

Despite Emery's keenness to sign Felix across multiple transfer windows, underpinned by the Spaniard's belief he could revive the stuttering career of the 2019 Golden Boy, a deal never came to fruition.

Felix, 26, now plies his trade with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia.

Emery's not-so-Rash decision

We now move to January 2025, where Villa had progressed to the knockout stage of the Champions League and were looking to finish the Premier League campaign strongly.

Marcus Rashford had been frozen out at Manchester United by then-manager Ruben Amorim.

Their relationship was so strained, Amorim said he would rather have his then-63-year-old goalkeeping coach Jorge Vital be among the substitutes over Rashford, who 'doesn't give the maximum every day'.

6 Rashford registered 10 goal contributions in 17 games for Villa Credit: Getty

But Emery spotted an opportunity to get a forward blessed with remarkable pace and quality back to his best.

"My challenge with him is huge," Emery said after Rashford moved to Villa on loan until the end of the season.

Marco Asensio, who Emery unsuccessfully pushed to sign in the summer of 2023, also arrived on loan.

Asensio, a three-time Champions League winner with Real Madrid, chose Paris Saint-Germain over Villa in 2023 but had struggled for game time with the French side.

Working under Emery ultimately proved to be a wise move for Rashford.

He quickly regained his spot in the England squad and spent last season on loan with Barcelona, although he is somewhat back to square one after they opted not to make the move permanent.

6 Rashford assisted four of Asensio's goals for Villa, proving Emery's restorative powers Credit: Getty

Villa did attempt to re-sign Asensio after his loan spell ended but could not complete a deal, as the attacking midfielder eventually moved to Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

The Don

The summer of 2025 brought yet another high-profile name, at least on paper, to Villa Park.

Jadon Sancho joined Manchester United from Borussia Dortmund in July 2021 for an estimated £73m.

It was a monumental fee for Sancho, who was just 21 years old at the time.

But - there's a theme here, isn't there - the big-money switch did not go to plan for either party.

After two seasons where he struggled to live up to the lofty price tag, Sancho's woes with United came to a head in September 2024 when the forward was forced to train away from the first team until a 'squad discipline issue' was resolved.

6 In the last three seasons, Sancho has scored just nine goals Credit: Getty

Mixed loan spells with Dortmund and Chelsea followed before he wound up at Villa on deadline day.

However, the 26-year-old struggled to make his mark under Emery, registering one goal and three assists from 39 appearances across all competitions.

Sancho was later released by United and remains a free agent.

Garna do it once more?

Which brings us to this transfer window, where Emery is, yet again, about to embark on yet another resurrection act.

This time, it's Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho, who is poised to join Villa on loan but with a conditional obligation to buy clause.

Emery previously tried to land the Argentinian last summer when it was clear he had no future at Old Trafford, only for Garnacho to join Chelsea instead.

6 With Morgan Rogers joining Chelsea, Garnacho has been pushed further out the exit door Credit: Getty

But the Blues are already looking to offload Garnacho after just one season in which he scored eight goals and assisted four.

Given the timing of Garnacho's potential move compared to the deadline day rush of Sancho, Emery's fingerprints are all over this deal and there's a high chance the winger would slot straight in to Villa's starting line-up.

Yet it's one that former Premier League stalwart Kevin Nolan couldn't quite wrap his head around, even if Emery backs himself to revive the 22-year-old.

Nolan, who admitted he doesn't know Garnacho personally, said: "He looks like a problem child, he looks like a problem if he's not playing, he'll throw his toys out of the pram if it's not going too well for him.

"I think if you've got him on board and you've got your arm around him and everything else and if everything suits him, I think he's a real big and good player.

"But is he big enough for Unai Emery to sort of go, 'I'll take him because I'll be able to get the best out of him?'"

6 Emery has backed himself to get the best out of Garnacho, who scored once in the league last term Credit: Getty

At age 22, time is certainly on Garnacho's side to prove his doubters wrong and enjoy a prosperous career.

But that relies heavily on Emery successfully performing yet another revival act.

If the Villa boss can do just that, it might be one of his best managerial feats yet.

Sports.title: Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals
Sports.content:
Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals

Premier League clubs have been hard at work splashing the cash this summer, with three clubs already completing nine-figure deals.

The transfer record for a British player has been broken with Chelsea sealing the £117million capture of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.



11 Rogers has joined Chelsea in a blockbuster deal

The 2026 summer window officially opened on June 15, with talkSPORT.com already providing a completed list of every deal.

Due to certain PSR constraints, some initial-loan agreements in previous windows have since become permanent this summer.

The rising inflation in the transfer market also means relegation is no longer a signal for clubs to poach key players on the cheap.



With that in mind, teams have had to open up their chequebooks. Below are the top 10 most expensive arrivals in the Premier League...

10. Luka Vuskovic (Tottenham to Brighton) – £46m

The Seagulls have built a reputation for signing young gems for moderate prices before later selling them on for big profits.



However, Fabian Hurzeler's men were forced to break their club record to prize Croatia defender Vuskovic from Tottenham.

The total deal for the 19-year-old includes bonuses that take the price above £50m, with the centre-back signing a five-year contract.



Spurs had previously knocked back two offers worth £30m and £35m for Vuskovic, who never played a competitive game in north London.

However, Vuskovic, labelled as a generational talent, underlined his standing as one of Europe's brightest young players while out on loan at Hamburg last season.

11 Vuskovic came head-to-head with England in Croatia's opening World Cup game Credit: Getty

9. Marco Palestra (Atalanta to Chelsea) - £47m

The Blues moved fast to hijack Inter Milan's move for the 21-year-old right-back, who has signed a six-year deal at Stamford Bridge.



The Atalanta academy graduate spent last season on loan at Cagliari and was named Serie A's defender of the year.

He scored once and registered four assists across 37 appearances in Italy's top-flight and is an ideal fit for Xabi Alonso's wing-back system.

Palestra made his senior international debut in March and earned his second cap in Italy's World Cup play-off final defeat to Bosnia.

The defender is already in Chelsea's first-team training and is expected to be part of their pre-season tour in Australia and Asia.



11 Palestra became the first signing of the Xabi Alonso era at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

8) Andrey Santos (Chelsea to Manchester United) – £50m

talkSPORT understands the Red Devils have paid £48m plus £2m in achievable add-ons to land the Brazilian midfielder from the Blues.

Newcastle were also understood to be keen on Chelsea's former No.17, who has now taken the same shirt number at Old Trafford.

The 22-year-old only made 13 Premier League starts last season, nearly half of which came under his ex-Strasbourg manager Liam Rosenior, during the latter's four-month tenure as Chelsea boss.



United prioritised central midfield reinforcements this summer following Casemiro's exit, with Manuel Ugarte also rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament at the World Cup.

11 Man United's new signing Andrey Santos made his unofficial debut against Wrexham in Helsinki Credit: Getty

7) Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton to Tottenham) – £52m

The Netherlands defender's move to Spurs wasn't part of the deal that saw Vuskovic head in the opposite direction.

However, on the balance sheet, Roberto De Zerbi reunited with his former Brighton player for a nominal fee, all things considered.



Tottenham were persistent in their bid to land Van Hecke, with Seagulls CEO Paul Barber revealing on talkSPORT that the Lilywhites had two previous bids rejected.

The Dutchman, who cost Brighton just £1.8m from NAC Breda in 2020, was entering the final year of his contract with Hurzeler's side.

11 De Zerbi has worked with the Dutch defender before on the south coast Credit: AFP

6) Johan Manzambi (Freiburg to Aston Villa) - £52m

Unai Emery's side have been involved in the biggest transfer of the summer so far, but have also broken their club record on a player.



The West Midlands club snapped up Manzambi for £52m, which surpassed the £50m forked out to land Amadou Onana in 2024.

Newcastle were close to signing the midfielder, having agreed a deal in principle with Freiburg for £51m, before Villa swooped in.

The 20-year-old played against Villa in the Europa League final, while he also scored three goals for Switzerland in the World Cup.

11 Villa broke their transfer record to sign the Switzerland midfielder Credit: Getty Images



5) Jeremy Jacquet (Rennes to Liverpool) – £60m

Liverpool completed the biggest deal of the winter window's deadline day by beating Chelsea to land the France U21 international.

talkSPORT understands that the Reds agreed an initial £55m to sign Jacquet, with a further £5m to be paid in potential add-ons.

A move for the defender eclipsed the £52m fee spent by Manchester City on Jeremy Doku in 2023 to become Rennes' record sale.

However, the 21-year-old spent the second half of last season at his boyhood club, with a move to Anfield only becoming official on July 1.



11 Jacquet inherited Ibrahima Konate's No.5 shirt at Liverpool Credit: Getty

4) Mateus Fernandes (West Ham to Tottenham) – £85m

Spurs have broken their transfer record twice this summer, the first of which saw Fernandes arrive from their relegated London rivals.

The 22-year-old was one of the standout Premier League midfielders last season, despite West Ham's struggles.

He scored five top-flight goals and registered four assists in 41 appearances but missed out on Portugal's World Cup squad.



However, Troy Deeney told talkSPORT that he questioned whether Fernandes was really the player to 'change the mentality' at Tottenham after his successive relegations, having also failed to beat the drop at Southampton.

11 Spurs beat off competition from Manchester United to secure Fernandes' signature Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

3) Sandro Tonali (Newcastle to Tottenham) – £100m

Spurs shattered their transfer record again to poach the Italian from Newcastle less than a week after unveiling Fernandes.

Tonali joined De Zerbi's side in a £100m deal - an initial £92.5m fee with £7.5m in proposed add-ons.



The 26-year-old made 110 appearances across his three seasons with Newcastle after his reported £52m move from AC Milan in July 2023.

But he was accused by talkSPORT Breakfast co-host Gabriel Agbonlahor of joining Tottenham 'for the big bucks'.

11 Tonali is the latest key player to leave St. James' Park after signing for Tottenham Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

2) Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) – £116m

Man City were the first of two clubs to break the transfer record for a British player following their capture of Anderson at the start of July.



The England international sealed his move to the Etihad Stadium from Nottingham Forest for a fixed £116m fee while at the World Cup.

Forest have tried to claim the deal is worth a total of £130m, which would eclipse the Premier League transfer record set by Liverpool's £125m signing of Alexander Isak, but City dispute this.

Anderson featured in all of England's games during their run to third at the World Cup - their best finish at the tournament since 1966.

11 Anderson put in some heroic midfield performances Credit: talKSPORT



1) Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa to Chelsea) - £117m

Anderson's reign as the most expensive British player lasted mere weeks as his England teammate Rogers took the crown.

The 23-year-old was the leading target at Arsenal, but he has now signed a six-year deal, with the option of another 12 months, at their London rivals Chelsea.

"I'm so excited," Rogers said on the move.

"For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

11 Rogers made three starts and a further four sub appearances for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty



"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here, and I can't wait to get started.

"The way the club wants to go and how it wants to move forward, it's something I want to be a part of, and I think it was just perfect for me.

"I'm a free spirit, free-flowing footballer. I like to take risks, make things happen, change games. Whatever that may take. Just can't wait to get started."

Sports.title: When is Champions League draw? Manchester United face club first in new European campaign
Sports.content:
When is Champions League draw? Manchester United face club first in new European campaign

The new Champions League campaign is already getting close as Europe's elite await the league phase draw.

Paris Saint-Germain beat Arsenal on penalties at the end of May to become back-to-back winners of the elite competition.



3 PSG won the Champions League last season with a penalty victory over Arsenal Credit: Getty

The 2025/26 final doesn't feel very long ago at all, but eyes are already moving on to the new season of action across Europe.

In fact, the new Champions League campaign has actually already started, with the qualifying rounds getting going in early July.

They will continue into August to decide the clubs that make it through to the full competition before the main draw.



Premier League champions Arsenal are going to be aiming to go one better this year, while Manchester City, Liverpool and Aston Villa will all be back in action in UEFA's elite competition again too.

Manchester United have also returned to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023/24 campaign.



It will be Man United's debut in the competition's new format, as they will be part of the league phase for the first time since its introduction by UEFA two seasons ago.

When is the Champions League draw?

The Champions League league phase draw will be held on Thursday, August 27 at UEFA's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland.



A start time for the draw is yet to be confirmed but will likely be 11am UK time.

The draw will include the 36 qualified clubs, with each team finding out their eight opponents for the league phase.

Each side will play four home games and four away games.

3 The 2026/27 league phase draw takes place at the end of August Credit: Getty

How to follow Champions League draw

talkSPORT and talkSPORT.com will be across all the latest news from the draw.



Listen talkSPORT through the website or find us on DAB digital radio through your smart speaker and on 1089 or 1053 AM.

Download and listen to all our live commentaries via the talkSPORT app.

For the latest odds and bet boosts for every big event, visit talkSPORT BET.

Subscribe to the talkSPORT YouTube channel for news, views and analysis plus our regular goals show and for more, 



The Champions League league phase draw is likely to be shown live on TNT Sports and HBO Max, as well as on UEFA TV.

Sports.title: West Ham star Crysencio Summerville set for £60m Saudi Arabia move despite Roma's late attempt to hijack deal - as Issa Diop makes £8.5m Premier League switch: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Roma's Summerville hijack plot fails

West Ham's Crysencio Summerville has accepted Al-Hilal's proposal.

Roma had made a last ditch effort to persuade the 24-year-old to join them but were told by West Ham they would have to increase their offer after Al-Hilal had a bid of £55m plus £5m in add ons accepted on Tuesday.

Garnacho heading to Villa

Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho on loan from Chelsea

The 22-year-old has been convinced by Unai Emery and joins on a loan with a conditional obligation to buy.

The Argentina international has travelled to Birmingham today to complete his medic and will sign a four year contract once the move becomes permanent.

Manchester United are due a sell on percentage.

Hull pushing to beat Ipswich for free agent Morita

Hull City have moved to try and beat Ipswich Town to the signing of Hidemasa Morita following his departure from Sporting Lisbon as a free agent.

Leeds United had also been in talks with the 31-year-old prior to the midfielder leaving the Portuguese side this summer.

Morita was a popular figure at Sporting, he played 31 times last season, and fans wanted him to stay but he now looks increasingly likely to join Premier League new boys Hull after their ambitious play to sign him.

Roma's last-gasp Summerville swoop

Roma have made a last-ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to choose them over Al-Hilal.

Coach Gian Piero Gasperini spoke to Summerville last night to try and convince him Roma's project was more suitable for the Netherlands international.

Al Hilal have agreed a £60m fee with West Ham with £55m up front.

Roma have made a last ditch attempt to persuade Crysencio Summerville to sign for them

Roma had offered £39m plus add ons.

The Italians are also keen on Chelsea defender Axel Disasi who was a teammate of Summerville's at West Ham last season.

They also made an offer for Chelsea's Alejandro Garnacho but Aston Villa's proposal for the winger offers more guarantees.

Wober departs Elland Road

Leeds United defender Maximilian Wober is joining Schalke on a free transfer.

The 28-year-old, who spent last season on loan at Werder Bremen, has been having a medical with Schalke.

Wober and Leeds are finalising a mutual agreement to terminate his contract a year early.

Valencia remain keen to sign Leeds attacking midfielder Largie Ramazani too.

Van Hecke completes Spurs move

Fellow Netherlands international Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton.

The Dutch centre-half, who chalked up three goals and three assists from 36 Premier League match for the Seagulls last term, had one year left on his contract at the Amex before Spurs swooped in to sign him.

It marks the latest signing in what has been a busy transfer window for Spurs, with Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Andrew Robertson, Martin Dubravka and Marcos Senesi all joining Roberto De Zerbi's ranks ahead of the new season.

Meanwhile, Middlesbrough have confirmed the signing of striker Will Lankshear from Tottenham in a deal worth £20million including add-ons.

He has signed a five year contract and said: 'Middlesbrough is such a massive club over the years; I deem it to be a Premier League club.

'The project here really excites me. I can’t wait to get started and be part of the journey, and get this club back where it belongs.'

Lankshear scored 11 goals in 43 appearances for Oxford United last season and also had interest from Wolves.

Jan Paul van Hecke has now completed his £52million move to Tottenham from Brighton

Tigers see £13.6m Danois bid rejected

Hull City have had a £13.6million bid rejected for Auxerre midfielder Kevin Danois.

The 22-year-old, who is also on Newcastle United’s watchlist, has emerged as a top target for Hull but Auxerre value him closer to £25million.

That would require Hull to smash their club transfer record and they want at least two new midfielders.

Danois is a France U21 international and made 33 appearances in Ligue 1 last term, scoring three times and registering one assist.

Liverpool's swoop for Monaco star comes up short

Liverpool made an approach for Monaco attacking midfielder Maghnes Akliouche early in the window.

The club checked on the potential availability of the 24-year-old but it was evident he was a prime target for Paris Saint-Germain.

PSG have made offers to Monaco for the France international but have still to agree on the fee.

Liverpool did not progress with talks after their initial check and are exploring other options including PSG's Bradley Barcola.

Wolves outcast Arokodare poised for swift exit

Ajax have joined the clubs showing interest in Wolves' wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare.

Arokodare will not be part of Wolves' squad to face Maidenhead tonight after his actions prompted coach Cesar Peixoto to cancel training on Monday.

The Nigerian refused to exit the training pitch when asked prompting the session to be cancelled. Extra security was then called in to the training ground on Tuesday to ensure the 25-year-old striker did not disrupt the session again.

Arokodare, who joined from Genk last summer, has been frustrated that his proposed loan move to Torino has not developed while Genoa have also made an enquiry.

Arokodare did not initially travel with the squad for last week’s warm weather training camp in Portugal, only receiving a late call-up following an injury to fellow forward Adam Armstrong.

In April, he faced disciplinary action after a dressing room bust-up with team-mate Mateus Mane during a 4-0 defeat at West Ham.

Wolves cancelled training after wantaway striker Tolu Arokodare refused to leave the pitch

Diop makes Premier League switch

Ipswich Town have confirmed the signing of Issa Diop from Fulham in a deal worth around £8.5m.

The centre-back has signed a four-year deal.

Ipswich schedule medical

Ipswich have also scheduled a medical for this week ahead of completing the £10million signing of Daizen Maeda from Celtic.

Ipswich agreed a deal for the forward worth an initial £8m plus £2m in add-ons.

Talks are continuing over a deal for free agent midfielder Hidemasa Morita, formerly of Sporting Lisbon, as well as Union SG’s Dutch goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen.
