TUESDAY: Fulham plot £24m bid for Southampton's Shea Charles... after Leeds have three bids rejected

MONDAY: New York meeting key to Chelsea's Maxence Lacroix move

SUNDAY: Roma ponder new bid for £50m-rated Crysencio Summerville

SATURDAY: Revealed: The figure Middlesbrough are set to pocket from Morgan Rogers' move to Chelsea

FRIDAY: Aston Villa sign Swiss World Cup star Johan Manzambi

Sports.title: Revealed: Rodri is pushing to sign for Real Madrid - and move from Man City could spark a midfield merry-go-round involving Man United target
Sports.content:
Revealed: Rodri is pushing to sign for Real Madrid - and move from Man City could spark a midfield merry-go-round involving Man United target

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City midfielder Rodri is waiting for Real Madrid president Florentino Perez to give the green light for his proposed return to Spain.

City have already signed Elliot Anderson and are working on a deal for Lille midfield prodigy Ayyoub Bouaddi, mindful that Rodri and his representatives have still to accept terms on the new contract they offered in April.

The 30-year-old, who has one year left on his City deal, is keen on a return to Madrid and there is growing support for the move on the back of him leading Spain to World Cup glory.

Perez was initially reluctant to back the transfer but others within the club have suggested it would be a good deal for the club and their image.

Jose Mourinho has been brought in to eradicate a perceived divisiveness in the Madrid dressing room and has already pushed for senior players to be recruited.

But the consequences could mean others departing.

Rodri is waiting for Real Madrid president Florentino Perez to give the green light to his return to Spain

Manchester United have not made fresh enquiries about Real Madrid star Aurelien Tchouameni

Aurelien Tchouameni has agreed a new contract extension and wants to stay in Madrid but could find opportunities become limited. Likewise, as Daily Mail Sport reported, his France compatriot Eduardo Camavinga could also yet depart.

As a result, Premier League clubs are attentive to the situation.

Daily Mail Sport understands that while Manchester United have a long-held interest in Tchouameni, they have not made fresh enquiries since their initial contacts months ago and established that the 26-year-old would also be very expensive and difficult to place in their current wage structure.

Camavinga has been considered by City, Chelsea and Arsenal. Despite his experience, he is still only 23. He could represent greater value but key is whether either would leave Madrid.

Other players expected to go are Gonzalo Garcia who is wanted by Fulham and Franco Mastantuono who will be allowed out on loan. Raul Asencio will also go as they work to recoup funds for Rodri and one more showpiece signing.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's full humiliation laid bare: Left crying as his Argentine thugs disgraced themselves... how this World Cup exposed the GOAT's dark arts shame

Like so many sporting greats, Lionel Messi did not get the fairytale ending that his illustrious career deserved in New Jersey on Sunday night.

Throughout history it has proven a rarity for legendary athletes to exit the big stage on a high. Muhammad Ali lost three of his final four fights before hanging up his gloves. Michael Jordan bowed out from the NBA after failing to make the playoffs for a second straight year with the Washington Wizards. Tom Brady waved goodbye to football after a postseason loss to the Dallas Cowboys.

Babe Ruth, Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal... the list runs long. And now Messi's name has been added to it. Well, at least when it comes to the World Cup.

The sad sight of Argentina's icon shedding tears after their final defeat to Spain says it all. At 39, it is almost certain this was his closing chapter on soccer's grandest stage. He will be 43 when the next one rolls around.

Yet Messi didn't just sign off from the World Cup on the back of a loss. It was as miserable and shameful of a night as it could be for his country at MetLife Stadium.

After becoming the first finalists in history to fail to register a single shot in 90 minutes - and not testing Spain's goalkeeper Unai Simon once in 120 - Argentina's sore losers resorted to thuggery when Spain celebrated their triumph at full-time.

Lionel Messi did not get his fairytale ending as Argentina lost to Spain in the World Cup final

The Argentina icon exited the biggest stage in soccer on the most depressing of notes

Midfielder Leandro Paredes was the biggest villain, grabbing Spain's Eric Garcia by the neck and punching midfielder Gavi in the face before pushing him over. Defender Nahuel Molina also punched Rodri in the torso, while even a 53-year-old Argentine assistant coach landed a punch on Spain's Dani Olmo.

While he was not involved in the violence, Messi is captain of this team and what will likely prove his World Cup finale will always be remembered for the ugly scenes at full time.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner didn't cover himself in glory, either. In the wake of a red card for Argentina's Enzo Fernandez, Messi embarrassed himself with an attempt to send Marc Cucurella down the tunnel.

After Cucurella spoke to him while briefly covering his mouth, Messi stuck his arm in the air and signaled to the referee to try and get the Spain man sent off. FIFA's new rules forbid players from concealing conversations.

Fortunately, the official did not bow to the pressure of one of the game's finest ever players. But the sight of an all-time great, renowned for modesty on and off the field, resorting to dirty tactics was grim.

'One of the most pathetic things I've ever seen from a supposed sportsman,' Piers Morgan fumed on X about the incident. 'Messi's fake halo shattered in this World Cup; he was the sneaky cheating leader of a vile bunch of violent thugs.'

Once they'd grown tired of lashing out, the now-former world champions made it a masterclass in bitterness by refusing to form a guard of honor for Spain and turning their backs as their competitors lifted the World Cup.

They then sparked ugly scenes at full time by lashing out at Spain as they celebrated the win

Leandro Paredes grabbed Eric Garcia by the neck and punching Gavi before pushing him over

Messi also embarrassed himself with his desperate attempt to get Marc Cucurella sent off

Cucurella briefly touched his mouth while talking to Messi - players are sent off for covering their face while talking to opponents

The closing shot of Messi at a World Cup will forever be crying with his back to the trophy lift, surrounded by his henchmen, in a moment more befitting of 10-year-old children than elite athletes.

If that wasn't bad enough, Argentina skipped mandatory post-game media interviews and fled the stadium.

Messi is known for humility while cementing his status as arguably the greatest of all time, with the petulant antics of famous rival Cristiano Ronaldo - often accused of hogging the limelight and not being a good teammate - painting him in a better light.

Nevertheless, soccer's golden boy bid farewell to the World Cup with most wanting him to lose. He did exactly that, without managing a shot on target before Argentina disgraced themselves.

Other than fan footage of her leaving the stadium under the protection of burly security guards, there were also mysteriously few sightings of Messi's stunning wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at Sunday's final.

It was a far cry from her usually-frequent appearances at the front of the stadium's VIP suites, cheering her man on alongside their children. How poignant, then, for her to be so far out of the spotlight as Messi struggled and wept on a devastating day.

There were few sightings of Messi's wife, Antonela Roccuzzo, at the final other than her leaving

It took Antonela a day before she paid tribute to her husband on social media after the loss

She broke her silence a day later, writing on Instagram: 'You will always be the best. Thank you for showing us every day that true success is built through hard work, sacrifice, and perseverance - without ever losing sight of who you really are.

'You are the best example for our children and an inspiration to millions of people. I admire you more than words can express, and I feel immensely proud to walk through life by your side.'

All in all, it was an anticlimactic end for the Messi family at his sport's most prestigious competition.

Even his all-time World Cup goals record no longer remains. Less than a month after leapfrogging Germany icon Miroslav Klose in Argentina's second group-stage outing against Austria, France superstar Kylian Mbappe's brace in the third-place playoff took him one ahead of Messi on 21.

So what next? Messi has half the season to finish with Inter Miami, who return to action Wednesday after MLS's World Cup break.

But Messi won't play in their first game back against Chicago Fire, nor their trip to CF Montreal on Saturday.

According to ESPN, he'll also skip the MLS All-Star Game on July 29, too. It would be the third time Messi has been selected for the annual showpiece. He is yet to play in a single one.

A more likely return is Miami's clash with Columbus Crew on Saturday August 1.

Once back up and running at club level, Messi has over two years remaining on his current deal with the team, which extends beyond the 2028 Copa America.

Messi may stick around at club level for a while but he will surely retire from Argentina duty

When he's still operating at such a high level - he still scored eight World Cup goals this year - it would be a shock to see him end that contract early.

As for his international career, it remains to be seen whether Messi calls it a day after two consecutive World Cup final appearances. It would make most sense.

Prior to the final he hinted as such by referring to it as 'The Last Tango' in a post on social media. Following the defeat, he also shared an emotional message on Instagram which felt like a farewell.

'The pain is immense, and this wound will take time to heal,' he wrote. 'But I also hold onto all the good things.

'Thank you from the bottom of my heart for every greeting and message. Once again, we managed to unite as a country and stand together, sharing the immense pride of being Argentine.'

Presumably through gritted teeth, he added: 'I also want to congratulate Spain on winning the championship.'

If only he and Argentina could have done a better job of that on the field.

Sports.title: Aston Villa agree Alejandro Garnacho deal: Ex-Man United star leaves Chelsea on loan with conditional obligation to buy
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

The 22-year-old has been convinced by Unai Emery and joins on loan with a conditional obligation to buy. Sources say the conditions are easily achievable and the total package meets the Blues' initial £40million valuation of the player.

The Argentina international has travelled to Birmingham today to complete his medical and will sign a four-year contract once the move becomes permanent.

Manchester United are due a sell-on percentage.

Aston Villa had made enquiries during conversations over Morgan Rogers’ £117m move to Chelsea.

Alejandro Garnacho has left Chelsea to join Aston Villa on loan with a conditional obligation

Roma had also offered a loan with options for Garnacho.

Garnacho had previously been of interest to Villa before he left Man United last summer.

The Argentine winger played 43 matches for Chelsea last season in all competitions.

Garnacho featured 24 times in the Premier League for the Blues, scoring one goal and providing three assists.

He scored eight times in total for Chelsea, with half of his goals coming in the Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Spurs fans fume at missing £85m new star Mateus Fernandes' wondergoal on 'pure garbage' in-house channel's coverage of pre-season friendly
Sports.content:
Tottenham fans have expressed their frustration after being unable to watch £85million signing Mateus Fernandes' superb goal in pre-season amid technical problems with the club's in-house TV channel.

Fans wanting to watch Tottenham's first pre-season match against MK Dons needed to tune in to their channel SPURSPLAY, which is carrying all of the club's pre-season matches.

The subscription is a benefit this season for the club's One Hotspur+ Members, while fans alternatively can pay £45 for an annual subscription or £35 if they are a One Hotspur member.

Fans had been looking to catch a first glimpse of their new midfield partnership of Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, who joined for £100m from Newcastle.

Fernandes opened the scoring just three minutes into the match, superbly volleying into the top corner from outside the box after MK Dons' goalkeeper had punched clear.

Tottenham's official X account shared the goal while highlighting that fans could watch on SPURSPLAY, prompting replies from fans already struggling with the service.

Tottenham fans were angered after missing £85m signing Mateus Fernandes' stunning goal in their opening pre-season match due to issues with the club's in-house channel

What a hit, Mateus Fernandes 💥



Watch our pre-season games live on SPURSPLAY! — Tottenham Hotspur (@SpursOfficial) July 22, 2026

Fernandes opened the scoring in Tottenham's pre-season match clash against MK Dons with a stunning volley from the edge of the area

'We can’t,' one fan responded while sharing a screenshot of the website that stated 'We are sorry, an error occurred. Please retry in a few minutes.'

'It seems this application has become very popular, and its available rate limit has been reached. Please retry in a few minutes,' an error message read.

One fan responded: 'This stream is running like pure garbage. If this doesn’t improve I will be demanding a refund.'

'I’d love to, but you won’t let me even though I paid my hard earned money. Well done,' a second added.

Another posted: 'Managing to get 10-15 secs then freezes. Every time. Were Spurs really not expecting massive interest considering they include Spursplay in the plus membership??,'

'How is it every season you fail to account for how many people might want to login and watch the friendlies. Seriously EVERY YEAR,' one fan said.

'Why is Spursplay stream not working? Only get still frames, anyone else had the same issue?' another added.

The friendly at Tottenham's Hotspur Way training centre is the club's first of their pre-season schedule.

Roberto De Zerbi's side will then travel to New Zealand to face Auckland FC on July 26, before taking on Sydney FC and Chelsea in matches on July 29 and August 1 in Sydney.

Tottenham then face Getafe and have two matches against Hoffenheim before beginning their Premier League season with a trip to Brentford on August 22.

Sports.title: Revealed: Lionel Messi's reputation among Brits PLUMMETS to staggering new low after Argentina's shameful World Cup campaign
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi's popularity among British people has plummeted after Argentina's shameful World Cup antics.

Messi is now viewed unfavourably among almost half of the participants surveyed by YouGov.

It comes after Argentina's baseless behaviour at the tournament, which ended with them losing 1-0 to Spain in the final and starting fights with the opposition. Enzo Fernandez was sent off in normal time and Leandro Paredes was lambasted for attacking Eric Garcia and Gavi after the match.

Even Messi was dragged into their pathetic antics in the final, attempting to get Marc Cucurella sent off for briefly putting his hand over his mouth.

As per FIFA's rules for this tournament, if a player holds their hand over their mouth in a confrontational situation, they will be sent off. That was the case with Paraguay's Miguel Almiron and Ecuador's Piero Hincapie. However, it didn't appear that Cucurella was speaking in a confrontational manner and neither the referee nor VAR decided to intervene.

Moreover, many supporters felt throughout the tournament that matches were 'rigged' to Argentina's benefit due to the quantity of refereeing decisions in their favour.

Lionel Messi's popularity among the British public has plummeted after the World Cup

His attempt to get Marc Cucurella sent off for a minor infraction was viewed as pathetic

And Argentina's players did not endear themselves to the English public by insisting that the Falkland Islands belong to them in a series of chants and banners.

All of this has had a deleterious effect on Messi's popularity.

Coming into the World Cup, he was viewed favourably by 55 per cent of the public and unfavourably by just nine per cent.

Now, he is seen favourably by only 29 per cent and unfavourably by 44 per cent.

That means that, according to YouGov's poll, Messi's net favourability rating among Britons has fallen from +46 to -15. In short, people don't like him very much.

His score is far worse than his arch-rival Cristiano Ronaldo, whose net rating is -2.

And he certainly lost his stock with Daily Mail Sport's veteran columnist Jeff Powell, who bunged Messi out of his top five all-time players for his antics.

In fairness, Messi, who scored eight goals throughout the World Cup, was often a beautiful and refreshing counterpoint to his more thuggish team-mates.

Messi avoided a red card for an apparent stamp during Argentina's first game vs Algeria

He also rose off the floor to shake Lamine Yamal's hand after the whistle on Sunday, when other team-mates were picking fights. Argentina also turned their backs on the victors during their trophy celebration.

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra-time thanks to a 106th-minute winner from Ferran Torres.

Any accusations of refereeing favouritism towards Argentina in the final were quelled by the sending-off of their midfielder Enzo Fernandez in the dying minutes of normal time.

But many people found it inexplicable that Spain's Nico Williams had a goal ruled out for a dubious foul on Nicolas Otamendi in the build-up.

That followed a pattern of questionable decisions made in favour of Argentina throughout the tournament.

Lionel Messi arguably should have been punished for a stamp in Argentina's first group match against Algeria - but he escaped a card entirely.

Messi, who scored a hat-trick in the match, caught Algeria captain Aissa Mandi on his right calf and Achilles tendon with his studs in a challenge after his first goal.

Algeria were given a free-kick by the referee but the incident was not even reviewed by VAR officials.

Meanwhile, Egypt reacted explosively after a string of critical decisions went against them in their last-16 match against Argentina.

Egypt manager Hossam Hassan furiously accused FIFA of rigging the World Cup after his side were knocked out by Argentina

Switzerland accused referee Joao Pinheiro of giving Argentina 'every decision'

Lautaro Martinez avoided a booking for jumping into the crowd after scoring his goal against Switzerland

First, forward Mostafa Ziko had a goal ruled out after a VAR review because of an apparent foul by Marwan Attia on Lisandro Martinez. That foul had occurred 18 seconds before at the other end of the pitch. Attia definitely caught Martinez - the debate is over whether not giving anything was a clear and obvious error.

What Egypt were more furious about is the build-up to Argentina's winning goal. They contend that they should have had a penalty at the other end moments before.

Mohamed Salah was brought down inside the box after having his foot clipped by Julian Alvarez, but VAR did not even seem to check the incident. Argentina had gone the other end and scored, in stoppage-time no less - but Egypt should admit that their defending was shoddy.

Pharaohs manager Hossam Hassan was apoplectic in his post-match interview. 'We were better, but football is unfair,' he said.

'It could be a matter of marketing, they could want to make a World Cup with the champion of the last World Cup, they want Messi to exist (in the tournament).

He added later: 'Why isn't there any fairness in sport? In football? I do not want to try to put it nicely here with beautiful wording. We have been treated unfairly today. We have suffered injustice.'

Moreover, Switzerland were incandescent after their quarter-final defeat by Argentina, accusing the referees of being 'one-sided' and 'against' them.

The major controversy of the match is the dismissal of Breel Donald Embolo with a second yellow card after diving.

Join the discussion Has this World Cup changed your opinion of Lionel Messi?

Argentina consistently referred to the Falkland Islands throughout the World Cup

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes was initially given a yellow card for a foul on Embolo. However, referee Joao Pinheiro was then instructed to review the decision by VAR under a new 'mistaken identity' rule.

The review showed that Embolo had initiated the contact with Paredes, leaving his right leg trailing to make contact with the Argentine, before tumbling to his left. The rule allows for a decision to be changed in the event a player has been booked or sent off, but the infringement was actually committed by the opposition.

Embolo was the one at fault for simulation, and so he was shown a second yellow. The striker was in tears after becoming the first player to be caught out by the rule, but it was clearly the right call.

Nevertheless, after the game, multiple figures from the Swiss camp stepped forward to air their grievances.

Granit Xhaka said: 'If you have to lose because of one decision from the referee, it’s painful but it was his decision. It’s difficult to accept now after a game because the dressing room was very quiet, disappointed. If you are disappointed after the game against this Argentina team, it shows a big mentality.

'The rules are the rules and we can’t change them but it’s a decision where you kill the game. That’s my opinion. I don’t know what else he can do but just don’t kill the game. We were so good in the game. I believed that at 11 versus 11 we would have had them but it’s very difficult to find the right words after the game.'

Defender Manuel Akanji said: 'When you have the referee against you, it becomes difficult. Every little thing was called against us. Every dive and every foul by the Argentinians went unpunished. I don't usually say anything against the officials, but I've never experienced such a one-sided game as today.

'As soon as the game was over, I thought: I'm so proud of our team. What we've achieved throughout the entire tournament, and especially today... We played against the world champions, and they didn't stand a chance.

FIFA have strenuously denied accusations of 'rigging' the World Cup in Argentina's favour

'I can't recall a single scoring opportunity from open play where we were lucky. If the game had continued 11 against 11, it would have likely gone in our favour.'

Team-mate Remo Freuler said: 'We had high hopes and put in a superb performance until the red card. That, of course, disrupted our flow. I still don't understand how VAR can intervene in such a situation. FIFA needs to explain that to me.'

Manager Yakin added: 'After the equaliser, we clearly had the momentum on our side. Unfortunately, this was punished by a refereeing error. The referee shouldn't have given the Argentinian a yellow card in that situation.

'There's no reason for it; the incident wasn't malicious or rough or anything like that. Then he corrects his own mistake and punishes us. That's incomprehensible and beyond my comprehension.

'The decision is baffling to me, there was no reason for it. It's a shame.'

Finally, Argentina have so far avoided punishment from FIFA despite their repeated chants referring to the Falkland Islands.

FIFA's rules strictly prohibit political chanting, slogans, and banners inside tournament venues. Haiti were forced to remove a small reference to their independence war on their kits just days before the tournament.

After the semi-final against England, Argentina's players held up a banner saying that 'Las Malvinas son argentinas' - The Falklands are Argentine. They may face disciplinary action for this, but didn't ahead of the final against Spain.

The Argentinians even got support from the US government over that. Andrew Giuliani, the head of the White House FIFA task force, said: 'We believe in our First Amendment rights here in the United States of America.'

Trust has been low in FIFA for a long time and their decision to suspend USA forward Folarin Balogun's ban so that he could play against Belgium after a phone call from Donald Trump did not help to restore confidence.

Sports.title: VOICE OF THE PADDOCK: Why George Russell can no longer assume he'll be treated fairly by Mercedes - as Toto Wolff lavishes Kimi Antonelli with praise (and a functioning car), while the Brit is left flailing
Sports.content:
VOICE OF THE PADDOCK: Why George Russell can no longer assume he'll be treated fairly by Mercedes - as Toto Wolff lavishes Kimi Antonelli with praise (and a functioning car), while the Brit is left flailing

Read Jonathan McEvoy, the Voice of the Paddock, every Monday on DailyMail+ - all the inside stories, analysis and exclusives you need to know from F1

You might not consider the following outburst a picture of restraint. It is not. But it was entirely called for. And it should not be the end of George Russell’s rigorous holding to account of his Mercedes team this week.

First, here is what Russell belted out over the team radio when his Belgian Grand Prix was condemned to end on the first lap, his pace falling off precipitously on Spa’s Kemmel Straight and leaving him to entangle himself with Lewis Hamilton.

‘I’m out,’ he screamed. ‘What the f*** happened with the SOC (state of charge) down the straight? Guys, unacceptable, unf***ing acceptable this whole weekend.’

Too right. Russell experienced two problems, which his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli entirely or partly escaped.

First, he ailed with a mysterious problem going back two races, concerning deployment from his battery. He talked of this after qualifying on Saturday, noting that not only was the issue unremedied but undiagnosed. The best his technical whizzes could do was rule out driver style as well as every other conceivable cause: tyres, excused; setup, excused; the whole scientific spectrum, excused. Thanks, guys.

Then, in Sunday’s race a separate gremlin, though one again attributed to a battery deployment limitation. Hence his reference to SOC, another acronym that might as well stand for the absurd complexity of these part-electric engines introduced so damagingly this year.

George Russell's outburst at Spa should not be the end of his rigorous holding to account of his Mercedes team

Russell's Belgian Grand Prix was condemned on the first lap, his pace falling off precipitously on Spa’s Kemmel Straight and leaving him to entangle himself with Lewis Hamilton

The bare fact is that Mercedes owe Russell an explanation for his problems in the lead-up to the Hungarian Grand Prix this coming weekend. His very title hopes are in the balance, the urgency of which situation his team principal Toto Wolff did not appear to grasp keenly enough in his post-race press conference in Belgium.

‘You have to understand that a driver is very emotional when these situations happen,’ said Wolff. He then added a gentle rebuke: ‘But as a Formula One driver you are part of a very elite group. And it is quite an honour to drive for Mercedes.

‘Sometimes we let ourselves down. I hope the numb feeling (Russell had disclosed he was numb to disappointment, so regularly had he experienced setbacks this season) goes away. We will try to recreate optimism and positivity.’

Perhaps behind closed doors, Wolff is incessantly urging his engineers to sort out the problem. If so, that is OK as far it goes. But making that clear to a wider audience would have conveyed a more uplifting message to Russell’s psyche, which is bruised by his falling 50 points back from world championship leader Antonelli, who has registered six wins to his two.

Yet, as is so often the case with the Austrian’s commentary on Russell, he could not bring himself to offer unequivocal backing.

Contrast his mealy-mouthed comments of Sunday night with how he sounded the trumpets for Lewis Hamilton, especially when he required some tender loving care in early 2022 as he recovered slowly from the trauma of missing out on the title to Max Verstappen in Abu Dhabi a few tormenting months earlier. Indeed, no half-decent Lewis drive passed without a gush of refulgent praise from Wolff. He applauds Russell’s achievements but with caveats strictly attached.

The manner in which Russell’s contract extension dragged on last year reflected this lukewarm pattern of half measures. He was kept dangling as Wolff toyed with signing Verstappen. He might instead have plumped for Russell from day one, and instead made Antonelli alone sweat it out for his place, the Italian being untried and prone to youthful mistakes. He could not bring himself to do that, and that tells us a lot.

Fast forward to this year. Antonelli has found his form and his confidence has soared. He is a talent and a half. But look at how much more enthusiastically Wolff and his deputy Bradley Lord salute Kimi’s latest reminder of his burgeoning strengths as they peer at the screens in the Mercedes garage. He seems to be their favoured project in a way Russell does not. The smiles are broader, and the fist clenching heartier.

Kimi Antonelli (left) seems to be the favoured project of Mercedes and Toto Wolff (right) in a way Russell does not

No half-decent Lewis drive passed without a gush of refulgent praise from Wolff. He applauds Russell’s achievements but with caveats strictly attached

As is so often the case with the Austrian’s commentary on Russell, Wolff could not bring himself to offer unequivocal backing

I do not believe for a moment that Russell is being sabotaged from within, whatever his most ardent online warriors may suggest – yet, for a moment, imagine the cacophony of doubts that would have been aired from vocal Hamilton blowhards if he were now in his successor’s predicament.

Deliberately undermined, no. But, still, George must cultivate the team for himself and not rely on what he recently told me, namely that he knew he must be being treated fairly because all 1,000 staff at the factory are on a bonus if they clinch the constructors’ title (standard at all teams), regardless of who wins out between him and Antonelli. Why, he argued, would they therefore care which driver prevails?

The logic is sound as far as it goes. But, of course, it is not that simple. Teams pull one way or another based on the relative performance of their drivers and by whichever of the pair plays the leadership game more adroitly off the track.

John Watson, who won five grands prix including from further back at Long Beach in 1983 than any winner in history, could race a bit. But he told me: ‘I thought it essentially came down to how you drove the equipment you had.

'Niki Lauda understood what I did not realise early enough in my career, which is that you had to get everything and everybody in the team working for you and, by whatever means available to you, build the car absolutely as you wanted it to be. My failure to see this clearly cost me in the end.’

There is a lesson in those sage words for George, who can at least help himself even if others are reluctant to do so.

Mosley and his shady, anti-democratic coterie would never rest

Poor old Max Mosley. The former president of the FIA dedicated the last years of his controversial life to muzzling a free Press to no avail, before blowing his brains out while dying of cancer in 2021.

Embarrassed by his exotic orgies creating front-page news, he not only sought to close the News of the World (successfully) for publishing their expose but also to bankrupt the Daily Mail.

Sir Ron Dennis, McLaren’s then owner and chairman, who was mercilessly tormented by Max Mosley, hit the nail on the head of the former FIA president

Mosley (right) bankrolled the Hacked Off zealots - a pointless waste of money his fascist father Oswald (centre) handed down, partly accrued from the family’s Nazi friends

This month’s High Court judgement entirely clearing the Mail of phone hacking, blagging and all other nefarious practices, rendered his demented bankrolling of the Hacked Off zealots a pointless waste of money his fascist father Oswald handed down, partly accrued from the family’s Nazi friends.

Mosley, I can reveal, was not always disdainful of this newspaper and once asked me at a black tie event in Monaco if I could arrange a dinner with our then-editor Paul Dacre, whom he described ingratiatingly that night as the ‘Dean of Fleet Street’. I never got round to Mosley’s request to break bread.

Would a Mosley-Dacre summit have cleared matters up before an oil slick of preening lawyers filled their bank accounts in a frothing crusade against the Mail? I categorically doubt it. There was a vengeful single-mindedness to Mosley behind his veneer of high-born urbanity.

In typically stiletto form, he once convened a lunch on Lower Regent Street to lampoon Sir Jackie Stewart as a ‘certificated halfwit dressed up as a 1930s music hall man’.

He was never going to let his vendetta against the Press rest, instead willingly writing out cheques for Hugh Grant and his shady coterie of anti-democratic conspirators.

I remember Sir Ron Dennis, McLaren’s then owner and chairman, who was mercilessly tormented by Mosley, asking me rhetorically once: ‘Do you honestly think it is possible that Max is only sadistic in his private life?’

And, with that observation, Dennis closed his case for the prosecution.

Catch on, Lando

Who is invading whose privacy is the first question that came to mind when Lando Norris complained of cameras tracking his recent nocturnal excursions.

Lando Norris (left) was none too happy about being papped leaving a London nightclub with influencer Alix Earle (right)

The world champion most strongly objected to a paparazzo tracking him across London by day. One understands this might be unnerving. There are rightly laws in place to protect an individual’s privacy and they should be enforced.

Yet Lando is surely not so wet behind the ears, or so far up an ivory tower, as not to contemplate the notion that hanging out with, and possibly dating, a glamorous American influencer comes with attendant risks.

Alix Earle, for it is she, can hardly carp about close attention. After all, publicity is the oxygen of her existence. She inhabits a make-believe world in which self-promotion is everything. Her curvaceous pictures on Instagram hardly dispel such views.

Is it, therefore, beyond the realms of comprehension that she or her ‘team’ tip off photographers about her whereabouts, and thus Lando’s too? It is a question he might care to consider.

Sports.title: Inside Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea exit: The game that sealed his fate, why Aston Villa target is happy to leave - and what Cobham insiders made of 'misunderstood' personality behind the scenes
Sports.content:
Inside Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea exit: The game that sealed his fate, why Aston Villa target is happy to leave - and what Cobham insiders made of 'misunderstood' personality behind the scenes

Unlock more from Kieran Gill inside the Chelsea camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Unai Emery had a front-row seat to see Alejandro Garnacho at his very best. The Aston Villa manager cut a frustrated figure in his technical area, watching while the winger reserved one of his finer performances for Chelsea in a 4-1 away victory at Villa Park in early March.

With Pedro Neto suspended, Garnacho exuded positivity throughout. Rarely did he seek to play a safe pass backwards. He was fast, direct, and unselfishly set up Joao Pedro to complete his hat-trick.

Our only gripe on the night was that Garnacho did not grab a goal for himself. He had enough opportunities while bursting beyond Emery’s back line.

Even so, Villa Park witnessed the potential of this player, who only turned 22 years old a few weeks back. There is an attacker who can influence games lying within, and if Villa are successful in signing Garnacho after agreeing an initial loan with a conditional obligation to buy, perhaps Emery could be the coach to coax that confidence out of him.

Neither Enzo Maresca nor Liam Rosenior nor Calum McFarlane were able to do so during his single season with Chelsea. Electric evenings like that one at Villa were rare. Those at Stamford Bridge were more used to seeing Garnacho struggle for form on their left wing, and there was one Premier League game in particular which impacted how his campaign ended.

That was in late January, when Chelsea were losing at home to West Ham and Garnacho had given up possession 10 times by the 32nd minute. He was hooked at half-time while his team were trailing 2-0. In the second half, they staged a comeback, winning 3-2 without him.

Alejandro Garnacho's Chelsea career is all but over after just one disappointing season, with Aston Villa primed to sign him

Former Manchester United star Garnacho started just two of Chelsea's final 14 Premier League games in 2025-26

In the 14 Premier League fixtures which followed that turnaround, Garnacho started only twice – one of those arriving at Villa. Both club and player came to the conclusion that it was not working.

Indeed, sources on both sides today say the decision for Garnacho to leave is mutual. It is not only that Chelsea want to find Garnacho a new home. Garnacho wants out of Chelsea, too.

The 22-year-old Argentinian sensed his status as surplus to requirements. The final reminder came in the last game of the season away at Sunderland. Garnacho never received word to remove his orange bib.

He remained an unused substitute in a match the visitors only needed to avoid losing to secure some form of European football. They lost 2-1 at the Stadium of Light.

As revealed by Daily Mail Sport earlier this month, Garnacho did not return for pre-season at Cobham alongside all of their other non-World Cup call-ups. That followed talks between him and Chelsea. He was told he could stay away while they worked on securing a transfer.

Despite his disappointing season, there was belief inside the club that the market was aching for wingers like him. Chelsea were prioritising a permanent sale while speaking with Serie A side Roma, but then Villa came along, with Garnacho and Nicolas Jackson’s names raised during their talks for Morgan Rogers.

Villa do not mind taking a chance on a player who has encountered an unfortunate patch in his career. They did so with Marcus Rashford and Jadon Sancho. The only concern for Chelsea might be that Villa did not then sign either of those players permanently, and the same goes for Harvey Elliott, the Liverpool loanee who was practically held hostage by his own conditional obligation – of 10 appearances – last season.

Garnacho was only signed by Chelsea from Manchester United last summer. He turned down an approach from Saudi side Al Nassr in that window. There was also an enquiry from Bayern Munich before they signed Luis Diaz, and – as a reminder of Emery’s long-term respect – Villa. Chelsea paid a fixed fee worth £40million with no add-ons, and United retained a 10 per cent sell-on clause.

Chelsea tried to help Garnacho along the way. Liam Rosenior (left) felt a particular need to try to protect his player, sensing he was someone who preferred an arm around him

Garnacho celebrates after forcing an own goal from Arthur Okonkwo in Chelsea's FA Cup win at Wrexham in March - but positive moments were few and far between last term

Employees at Cobham were unsure what to expect with Garnacho. Like all of us, they had heard the stories, had seen how it ended at United, and were aware he arrived with a reputation.

Yet speak to those sources today and you will find they rather liked the lad. He is described as shy and misunderstood, and we are reminded that he arrived at Chelsea at the age of 21.

He also turned up later than everyone else, without a pre-season behind him, and ended up playing under three head coaches in nine months. It was not an easy campaign in which to adapt to a new club.

Chelsea tried to help Garnacho along the way. Rosenior felt a particular need to try to protect his player, sensing he was someone who preferred an arm around him.

When asked at one press conference why Garnacho was booed wherever he went, Rosenior’s answer bordered on what your mum tells you when the bullies at school are being mean – jealousy. ‘I don't understand why that happens,’ Rosenior told us. ‘Maybe it’s because he can be such a threat.’

Chelsea put their player up for a Champions League press conference before playing Atalanta. That presser was only the warm-up. The club then arranged a sit-down interview with Premier League Productions to tell his story and to his credit, Garnacho came across as sincere, or a ‘normal guy’ as he described himself.

He discussed being a humble father to his two-year-old son Enzo, and conceded he had made mistakes – presumably referring to his social media presence, like when he wore a Villa shirt with fellow outcast Marcus Rashford’s name on the back.

Now, he could be wearing a Villa shirt all over again, now the clubs have reached an agreement on a loan move.

Aston Villa boss Unai Emery doesn't mind taking a chance on a player who has encountered an unfortunate patch in his career. He did so with Marcus Rashford (pictured)

Speak to those sources at Cobham and you will find they rather liked Garnacho. He is described as shy and misunderstood

It is naturally a curious link, given both Chelsea and Villa are working under financial restrictions with UEFA, who would scrutinise any deal struck for Garnacho so soon after Rogers headed in the other direction for £117m. They can bet other clubs will be watching what happens closely, too.

Per UEFA’s written rules, if a conditional obligation in a loan is considered to be ‘virtually certain’, then the temporary transfer must be categorised as a permanent one from the offset. It would need to be seen as genuinely conditional in the eyes of European football’s governing body.

Villa could, of course, argue that their loan arrangement for Elliott may have appeared ‘virtually certain’ – he only had to play 10 Premier League games to be bought permanently from Liverpool for £35m – but it was never triggered.

Whatever happens, Chelsea and Garnacho realise their time together is up, after a season in which they learned they were not suited for one another.

Sports.title: Cameron Menziesu urgently treated by medics and out of World Matchplay after scary incident
Sports.content:
Cameron Menziesu urgently treated by medics and out of World Matchplay after scary incident

Action at the World Matchplay had to be suspended during Cameron Menzies' clash with Ross Smith as the former was taken off stage to receive medical attention - later withdrawing

View Image Cameron Menzies was helped off the stage during his match with Ross Smith

Play at the World Matchplay in Blackpool had to be halted after Cameron Menzies was forced to leave the stage to receive medical attention - leading to his withdrawal from the tournament.

‌



He was leading Ross Smith 2-1 but the fourth leg of their contest was put on hold. Before Menzies slumped over he was swaying on the stage, which caught the attention of those around him. He looked as if he was feeling faint before his discomfort became obvious.

‌



Sky Sports presenter Emma Paton said: "We are having a break in our first match because Cameron Menzies is unwell. All we know at the moment is that he is being seen to by St John's Ambulance. He is with some medics at the moment. Hopefully he is ok and feeling better very shortly."

‌



Mark Webster added on the incident: "Smith was obviously concerned. He'll be offering his support. While the medics are seeing to Cameron, he's got to stay on the practice board. But ultimately it's just about hoping that Cameron is okay at the minute."

Smith has ultimately progressed to the quarter-finals as a result of Menzies' unfortunate illness. After Menzies' withdrawal the night's second match - Gian van Veen vs Wessel Nijman - has been bought forward.

Sports.title: Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot
Sports.content:
Aidan O'Brien compares Benvenuto Cellini to Galileo ahead of King George at Ascot

Benvenuto Cellini is the 11-4 second favourite for the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes at Ascot on Saturday, with trainer Aidan O'Brien drawing comparisons to his legendary grandfather Galileo

View 3 Images (Image: Alan Crowhurst, Getty Images)

Aidan O'Brien has drawn a comparison between Benvenuto Cellini and the colt's legendary grandfather Galileo, possessing all the same class and courage but "probably" a touch more pace, as he chases a first King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes triumph since 2016.

‌



The three year old is looking to build on his Irish Derby victory with a winning display at Ascot this weekend, a race Galileo himself won during his Classic year back in 2001.

‌



And while it represents the sternest examination of his career against a stellar line-up of older rivals, O'Brien is convinced the son of Frankel has every attribute needed to become only the seventh three year old winner of the race this century.

‌



Cheltenham Festival veteran Edwardstone retired after finishing career on a high READ MORE :

"We think he's a very high-quality, classy horse on fast ground. He's probably a bit quicker than Galileo was, but he moves like him and we think he's brave like he was too," he said.

"There's no better mile-and-a-half race anywhere. It's a difficult race, usually run on fast ground and it's run at Ascot too, which is a very special place. You need a horse that stays.

"They have to have class and it's where the three-year-olds meet the older horses for the first time (at the trip)."

‌



Benvenuto Cellini will need to get the better of not only race favourite Calandagan but last year's runner-up Kalpana, Japanese star Masquerade Ball and stablemate and Arc runner-up Minnie Hauk, to name just four of what could be a field of ten.

View 3 Images Galileo (left) with jockey Michael Kinane wins the King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Diamond Stakes from Fantastic Light and jockey Frankie Dettori at Ascot today, Saturday 28th July 2001. **EDI** PA Photo : Tim Ockenden

O'Brien acknowledges he is unleashing two genuine contenders as he attempts to secure a prize he has claimed four times previously, with Dylan Thomas (2007), Duke Of Marmalade (2008) and Highland Reel (2016) joining Galileo's triumph.

‌



Minnie Hauk produced an excellent second behind Ombudsman in the Prince of Wales's Stakes last time out, a performance O'Brien believes will have set her up perfectly for the step back up to 12 furlongs.

"We ran her in the Prince of Wales's Stakes with a view to coming back for the King George, and we thought that was probably her best run ever. The extra couple of furlongs should really suit her," the trainer said.

Following her runner-up finish behind Daryz in Paris last October, Minnie Hauk concluded her campaign with a sixth-place effort behind Ethical Diamond in the Breeders' Cup Turf at Del Mar in California.

‌



View 3 Images Minnie Hauk has been backed to run well in the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes (Image: ©INPHO/Morgan Treacy)

Both the filly and Benvenuto Cellini could share the same objective, with the King George guaranteeing entry into the field for the Breeders' Cup Turf at Keeneland at the end of October as part of the Breeders' Cup 'Win and You're In' series.

O'Brien explained: "The Breeders' Cup is massive. We went there last year (with Minnie Hauk) and got things wrong tactically. You can't go anywhere better, it's where all the horses meet. It's very competitive racing at good tracks and the atmosphere is second to none.

Article continues below

"Benvenuto Cellini could go too. He's a horse that will enjoy travelling and he's a great mover. He would be fine coming back to a mile and a quarter, and I think you need that kind of pace at the Breeders' Cup.

"He's an easy horse to train who doesn't take a lot of work so it could suit him perfectly."

Sports.title: From beach cleaning to the Commonwealth Games: Artist hopes King's baton raises awareness of threat of ocean plastic
Sports.content:
From beach cleaning to the Commonwealth Games: Artist hopes King's baton raises awareness of threat of ocean plastic

A King's Baton made from discarded plastic will carry a powerful environmental message into this week's opening ceremony in Glasgow.

View 2 Images Cornish artist Bonnie Steward designed Team England's King's baton for the Commonwealth Games.

From beach rubbish to centre stage at the Commonwealth Games.

‌



A King's Baton made from discarded plastic will carry a powerful environmental message into this week's opening ceremony in Glasgow. Cornish artist Bonnie Steward created Team England's Baton from rubbish collected on beaches, riverbanks and in towns in the hope of highlighting the growing threat of ocean plastic.

‌



Her striking artwork will be showcased before King Charles and Queen Camilla at the opening ceremony inside Glasgow's OVO Hydro. The 27-year-old, from Crowntown, near Helston, transformed crisp packets, pieces of fishing rope, fragments of tennis balls and other discarded waste into colourful mosaics depicting England's best-known landmarks and landscapes.

‌



Tower Bridge and the Angel of the North feature alongside coastal views inspired by her Cornish home, with every piece of plastic collected from the places represented in the design.

Steward said: "Literally every single piece, a crisp packet, a part of a tennis ball or a piece of fishing rope, everything you see, I've collected. On the King's Baton, there are pieces from the Thames foreshore, from our own shores and urban areas.

"I hope people understand that ocean plastic is not just a beach issue."

‌



View 2 Images The King's baton designed by Bonnie Steward.

Steward, who founded her BISH ART business in Cornwall, began collecting plastic after becoming increasingly alarmed by the amount of rubbish washing ashore near her home.

She said: "Growing up on the Cornish coastline, I became increasingly saddened by how much plastic was being washed ashore. I started collecting it because I couldn't ignore it, and I quickly became obsessed with beach cleaning."

‌



Her artwork is designed to resemble a painting from a distance, before revealing the individual pieces of waste when viewed up close.

Steward added: "What I like about creating my work is that when people view it, they think it's a painting at first glance. But the closer they look, they notice all the elements. It's almost like a puzzle."

For the first time, each Commonwealth nation received its own baton to personalise ahead of Glasgow 2026. Steward said working on such a small scale presented a new challenge, but she was determined to create something that represented the whole country.

Article continues below

She said: "I've never worked at such a small size before, so every detail had to count.

"What mattered most was creating something people could connect with, something familiar and an artwork that was reflective of England as a whole. As an artist, you rarely imagine your work being carried by athletes across the nation, so to see the Baton out in the world is surreal."

Sports.title: 'Really exciting' - Swimmer Luke Greenbank selected to carry Team England baton at Glasgow 2026 Opening Ceremony
Sports.content:
'Really exciting' - Swimmer Luke Greenbank selected to carry Team England baton at Glasgow 2026 Opening Ceremony

The swimmer is heading to his third Commonwealth Games and will start by leading his country out at the Opening Ceremony

View 2 Images Team England swimmer Luke Greenbank will be carrying the baton at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games opening ceremony. (Image: imagecomms/Team England)

Luke Greenbank knows only Commonwealth gold will outdo the honour of being selected as Team England’s baton bearer at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games.

‌



The 28-year-old will carry his country’s baton at Thursday’s opening ceremony alongside flagbearer Sian Honnor. Greenbank heads to his third Games and after a disappointing showing at Birmingham 2022, where the Olympic bronze medallist missed out on individual honours, the Cockermouth swimmer is confident that his best is yet to come as one of the most experienced members of the swimming squad.

‌



He said: “At Gold Coast, I was the newcomer and didn't really know what to expect. In Birmingham, I probably put too much pressure on myself and didn't get the performances I wanted.

‌



“This time, I feel really confident coming into the Games. I don't put as much pressure on myself anymore and I'm a more experienced athlete. I'll be a bit calmer and hopefully that leads to some good results.

“Compared with my first Games, I'm much more mature and experienced. I understand what a major sporting event looks like and how to handle myself. I've learned a lot from previous Commonwealth Games, Olympics and World Championships. Once you've experienced enough of them, it becomes second nature and you don't feel the same pressure because it's just another swim.

“I've never won an individual Commonwealth medal, so that's a massive aim for me and a really big motivator. I don't want to put too much pressure on that. I just need to focus on what I have to do to produce the best performance possible.”

‌



Greenbank won 4x100m medley silver on the Gold Coast before upgrading to gold in Birmingham but before Greenbank takes to the pool, he will represent his country at the opening ceremony in the new baton-bearer role. It is particularly poignant for Greenbank, having been given the nod by his fellow athletes.

View 2 Images Luke Greenbank.

He added: “To be nominated as flagbearer is really exciting. It's not something swimmers usually get to experience because we're competing from day one, but because my events are a little later in the programme, I'll be able to attend. It'll be a great experience and I'm really proud to represent the team. I knew I had been nominated by Swim England, but I wasn't really expecting anything.

‌



“Then at a team meeting I was told by the Team England staff. It was a really nice moment to be selected by the athletes and represent them at the opening ceremony.”

With the Games taking place in Glasgow, the Cumbrian’s friends and family have a shorter journey than most other English supporters and he is relishing the extra support in his bid for individual glory.

“It's probably closer for me here than Birmingham [2022] was, which is funny,” he said. “It'll be great to have friends and family in the crowd. My mum and dad are coming up, as is my fiancée, Anna. I'm really excited and hopefully I can put on a good show for them.

Article continues below

“The key is to keep a cool head, stick to the race plan and trust the training. Training has been going really well recently, so I can't let anything get into my head too much. The hard work is done now.”

Sports.title: Sir Chris Hoy backs Glasgow to put on a show as host city at Commonwealth Games
Sports.content:
Sir Chris Hoy backs Glasgow to put on a show as host city at Commonwealth Games

Hoy was in Glasgow ahead of the Games to celebrate the impact of funding from The National Lottery in the city.

View 3 Images Scottish Cycling Legend Chris Hoy. (Image: SNS Group)

Sir Chris Hoy is backing Glasgow to get behind the Commonwealth Games in the same way it did 12 years ago.

‌



Glasgow stepped in as last-minute hosts for the 2026 edition after the Australian state of Victoria pulled out in 2023. Scotland’s biggest city has organised a scaled-down version of the Games from the one it hosted in 2014, but Hoy believes Glaswegians will embrace it all the same and put on a brilliant show for the rest of the Commonwealth.

‌



“I think it's gathering momentum now, definitely,” he said. “People can see it's almost here. The memories from 2014 are still relatively fresh, so people are excited to be able to do it all again.

‌



“I know we can do a great job this time around as well. All the facilities from those Games still exist, so we're all set and ready to go. We just need the public to get behind it, and I'm sure they will.

“The people love sport, the city loves sport, and this is a chance for them to demonstrate that passion. Glasgow has done a really important job in helping carry on the Commonwealth Games and hopefully steady the ship for the future.

“I don't think it's going to be substandard. It will obviously be on a smaller scale, but I think the quality will still be there in terms of the event.

‌



“I'm expecting it to be fantastic and for the locals to really get behind it in the way they did 12 years ago and welcome the entire Commonwealth to Glasgow.”

View 3 Images The Sir Chris Hoy Velodrome, one of the venues for this year's Commonwealth Games (Image: Daily Record)

Hoy will be part of the opening ceremony next Thursday, reprising a similar role to 2014 when he memorably helped the Prime Minister of Malaysia with a faulty baton. The six-time Olympic champion will also provide track cycling punditry from the velodrome that bears his name. On the track, he won two Commonwealth golds for Scotland in his only opportunities to wear the Saltire.

‌



“For me, it was the only chance to compete for Scotland, so it made it extra special to ride in the Scottish jersey,” he reflected. “It's a unique event, and the opportunity to hear the Scottish national anthem on the podium is something that stood out for me.

“The two moments I had to stand on the podium and receive a gold medal for Scotland were really special.

“There are a number of things that make the Commonwealth Games unique, and that is definitely one of them.”

‌



View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy was a guest in the Royal Box on day six of The Championships Wimbledon 2026 (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

Hoy was in Glasgow ahead of the Games to celebrate the impact of funding from The National Lottery in the city. Over £1 billion has now been invested in Scotland’s biggest city and the six-time Olympic champion was at charity Glasgow The Caring City to see first-hand the impact the money makes.

He added: “I'm genuinely blown away by it. There are fantastic people doing stuff for their community, and young people are benefitting from that. It's exciting, and we're building up towards the Commonwealth Games next week, highlighting all the benefits that sport and different projects have received from National Lottery funding.”

Sports.title: Man Utd given green light to complete transfer as forward 'says yes' to move
Sports.content:
Man Utd given green light to complete transfer as forward 'says yes' to move

Manchester United are looking to bolster their squad ahead of a return to the Champions League with the Red Devils considering signing a new striker

View 2 Images Michael Carrick's Manchester United side are gearing up for a return to the Champions League. (Image: (Photo by Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee is willing to join Juventus, which could see Michael Carrick's side head into the market for an attacking addition of their own. The 25-year-old started in United's pre-season curtain raiser against Wrexham last weekend but looks set to leave the club.

‌



The Dutch international has managed just 127 minutes of competitive football under Carrick since his return to Old Trafford. Despite struggling since his move to Manchester, there's been plenty of interest from Italian clubs having impressed at Bologna prior to his Old Trafford move.

‌



Several Serie A clubs are keen on signing Zirkzee this summer, with Juventus leading the race to sign him. The Old Lady appeared focused on signing Randal Kolo Muani, but talks with PSG have hit a stumbling point, forcing Juve into a rethink.

‌



Man Utd and Arsenal locked in £40million transfer battle as duo hold talks over deal READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

La Gazzetta Dello Sport now reports that Zirkzee has given an initial 'yes' to the prospect of joining Juventus and is attracted by the idea of returning to Italy. The Italian publication states that Luciano Spalletti's side would prefer an initial loan arrangement, while continuing to pursue Kolo Muani separately.

United would almost certainly favour a permanent sale of Zirkzee in order to reinvest the proceeds back into the squad, potentially funding a replacement, with the option of a deal incorporating an obligation to buy. Zirkzee had been eager to depart in January but was refused permission by United.

‌



View 2 Images Joshua Zirkzee could leave Man Utd this summer. (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Had that been approved, Benjamin Sesko would have been the sole recognised fit centre-forward, though he is currently recovering from a shin injury. While attention appears to remain firmly on midfield, United are also casting their eye over the striker market and weighing up their choices.

The most probable outcome points towards an experienced forward arriving - perhaps not the most headline-grabbing acquisition, but one well-versed in the demands of the Premier League. Karl Darlow, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos have already officially put pen to paper at the club, with a third midfield signing anticipated.

‌



AS Roma's Manu Kone and Bournemouth's Alex Scott appear to sit at the top of United's shortlist, though both players are attracting considerable interest from rival clubs. Chelsea even had a £64million bid for Scott rejected.

A new left-wing addition is also under consideration, with Crysencio Summerville and Iliman Ndiaye both linked, although the former appears destined for Saudi Pro League outfit Al-Hilal, who have had an offer accepted by West Ham. Marcus Rashford's future will have a bearing on any potential frontline reinforcement, though offloading Zirkzee could free up funds towards securing a forward capable of helping lead the line.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
