World.title: Jaishankar flags need for fair trade, supply chain reliability in meeting with Wang Yi
World.content:
External affairs minister S

underlined the significance of fair market access, trade balance and supply chain reliability in a meeting with his Chinese counterpart Wang Yi, while welcoming recent measures to normalise Sino-Indian ties like the upgrading of the visa framework and resumption of direct flights, Kailash pilgrimage and border trade.

In a meeting in Manila on the margins of ASEAN events, Jaishankar also stressed that border peace and tranquility will remain a prerequisite for normal ties. Ahead of the BRICS summit India will host in September, he thanked Wang for China's support for India's presidency. While a final confirmation from Beijing is still awaited, President Xi is likely to attend the summit.

India's relations with China have improved considerably since PM Narendra Modi and Xi met in Kazan in 2024, marking the end of the border standoff in eastern Ladakh.

However, for India, addressing economic friction in ties including over the asymmetrical $ 100 billion trade imbalance and the need for Indian manufacturing to reliably access Chinese raw materials remains an essential next step for broader normalisation.

According to official sources, India continues to raise issues related to trade restrictions imposed by Beijing and is working with the Chinese government to ensure predictability in supply chains for trade consistent with international practices.





"Fair market access and a trade balance ranks high in that regard. There are also concerns about predictability of supply chains. Facilitating both official and people-to-people exchanges merit our attention. We also need to agree on the meetings of various mechanisms and platforms as per our mutual priorities," said the minister in his opening remarks, underscoring the significance of the meeting in an extremely complicated global situation.

Jaishankar said that while both sides had engaged to ensure border peace since October 2024, this issue would continue to need constant attention and that relevant mechanisms in that domain had to be given full support and strong encouragement.

âIt is natural that as two large and important nations, and that too proximate neighbours, India and China would have their own particular interests. That is why our leaders had agreed that differences should not become disputes.

It is the responsibility of diplomacy to properly manage them,â said the minister.

The minister reiterated India's position that the bilateral relationship must be built around the "3 mutuals" or mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity.

"We believe that a stable and cooperative relationship can best be developed on the basis of mutual respect, mutual interest and mutual sensitivity," said Jaishankar, adding that such a relationship can make a valuable contribution to a multi-polar Asia and a multi-polar world.

The minister said that relations have been gradually normalising since the October 2024 Kazan Modi-Xi meeting and this was further affirmed when the leaders met in Tianjin last year. Modi travelled to Tianjin in August 2024 for the SCO summit.

World.title: Soldier slips to death in J&K’s Rajouri
World.content:
JAMMU: A 27-year-old Army jawan died after accidentally slipping from a height near the Line of Control (LoC) in J&Kâs Rajouri district on Wednesday.

The deceased, Rifleman Sukhpreet Singh, was a native of Punjab and posted with JAK Rifles.

He was on duty at Mahadev forward post in Sunderbani sector when he suddenly lost his balance and fell from a height, officials said.

The body was shifted to a hospital for post-mortem. Police launched inquest proceedings. The remains will be taken to his native place for the last rites, officials said.

In a similar tragedy last month, an Army officer died after slipping from a steep mountain ridge and plunging into a deep gorge on June 6 during Operation Sheruwali in Rajouri district. Lt Beereshwar Goswami was leading a search party along a narrow ridge when he lost footing and fell into the gorge. The anti-terror operation, which was launched in the dense forests of Rajouriâs Dorimal-Gambhir-Mughlan belt on May 23 to track two-three Pakistani ultras, is still underway.

World.title: Drone-assisted cross-border drug smuggling surges since 2021, Punjab worst hit: Government
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The home ministry on Wednesday said drone-assisted, cross-border drug trafficking has risen exponentially since 2021, with Punjab being the most affected state, accounting for 298 of the 305 countrywide drone-related drug trafficking incidents last year.

Replying to a question in the Rajya Sabha, junior home minister Nityanand Rai said nearly 460 kg of narcotic drugs, including 448 kg of heroin, 9 kg of methamphetamine and 3 kg of opium was seized in actions against drone-assisted trafficking.

âTrends of cross border narcotics infiltration reveal that drug trafficking syndicates operating across the border have increasingly been employing sophisticated methods such as drones, GPS-enabled consignments, encrypted communications and local receiver networks to infiltrate heroin, methamphetamine, arms and ammunition into India,â Rai informed the Rajya Sabha.

World.title: 6.7 crore saplings planted by CAPFs in last 5 years: MHA tells Parliament
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Central armed police forces (CAPFs) have planted nearly 6.7 crore saplings in the last five years as part of a countrywide plantation drive, the home ministry told the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday.

Junior home minister Nityanand Rai, in reply to a written question, shared that the seven CAPFs -- CRPF, BSF, CISF, ITBP, NSG, SSB and Assam Rifles -- also developed a total 3,212 nurseries between 2020 and 2025 and set up and dedicated 1,995 âvatikasâ to martyrs between 2020 and 2024.

A statewide distribution of the 6.9 crore saplings planted by the Central paramilitary forces in the last five years, shows north-eastern states at the top of the table. While Manipur saw the plantation of 64.8 lakh saplings, 61.2 lakh were planted in Nagaland and 59.6 lakh in Assam.

CRPF and BSF, between themselves, developed 69% of the nurseries developed by the CAPFs in the last five years, according to data shared by Rai. ITBP led in development of vatikas, having set up 763 in the period 2020 to 2024.

World.title: 37,164 killed on 6,358 ‘black corridors’ of NHs in 3 yrs: Road ministry
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Govt has identified 6,358 âblack corridorsâ on NH network during 2023-25, which recorded 37,164 deaths, as per road transport ministry. The maximum such black corridors were in Tamil Nadu (958), followed by UP (671) and Karnataka (607).

Among districts, Viluppuram in Tamil Nadu had a maximum of 70 such corridors.

Unlike isolated black spots, these corridors are continuous stretches of NH that have recorded a higher number of fatal and grievous road crashes. The identification is expected to help authorities prioritise engineering interventions and improve

outcomes, officials said.

The road transport ministry informed the Rajya Sabha on Wednesday that black corridors have been identified based on the available crash data from Electronic Detailed Accident Report (e-DAR).

As per ministry data, Pune Rural district had 60 black corridors, followed by 52 in Purba Medinipur in West Bengal, 49 in Cuddalore in Tamil Nadu and 48 in Palakkad in Kerala.

Responding to a separate question, road transport minister Nitin Gadkari informed the Upper House that govt has adopted a phased roadmap for deployment of advanced traffic management systems (ATMS) across all four-lane and above NHs and expressways.





The roadmap includes establishment of local, regional, and national command and control centres for centralised monitoring, incident management, traffic analytics, and coordinated response.

In a written reply to another question on highway quality, the ministry said major deficiencies in NH stretches and bridges since March 2024 have been reported for 61 projects and stretches across the country. The deficiencies included collapse and defects in reinforced soil wall, girders, concrete panel, rutting and potholes. It said that 103 contractors and agencies have been blacklisted and penalised for poor quality work.

World.title: 58% of IRCTC booking requests were automated, access denied: Railways
World.content:
NEW DELHI: In the past six months, nearly 58% attempts to book train tickets online were by bots, not real people, the railway ministry informed Lok Sabha Wednesday. It said that on average 888 crore requests out of 1,538 crore in a month were bots, and those were flagged as automated requests and their access to the e-ticketing system was denied.

A bot is an automated software application that performs repetitive tasks over a network. It follows specific instructions to imitate human behaviour at a faster rate. In a written reply, railway minister Ashwni Vaishnaw said that such âspurious attemptsâ that were denied access to e-ticketing systems was the maximum in June â nearly 66% of the 1,912 crore requests by bots.

âBot manager in the system protects websites at its own cloud servers by using user behavioural analysis, bot signature/ pattern matching, and real-time risk scoring to instantly distinguish humans and bots and software,â an IRCTC official said.

Vaishnaw said the train ticket reservation system is robust and highly secure, and equipped with industry-standard, state-of-the-art cybersecurity controls while highlighting measures taken by railways to safeguard the system from cyber attacks, and prevent auto-filling of forms by hacking tools to curb fraud in Tatkal ticket bookings.

The minister said that multiple protective layers such as network firewalls, intrusion prevention systems, application delivery controllers and web application firewalls have been deployed to safeguard the system against cyber threats.





He added that little over three crore suspicious user IDs had been deactivated and 6.2 crore had been placed under revalidation during 2025-26 and 2026-27 (up to June 30).

The ministry said that 503 complaints have been lodged on the National Cyber Crime Portal for suspicious booking and 13,343 suspicious emails have been blocked in the past one-and-half years. In addition, since 2021, Railway Protection Force has arrested 22,676 touts and legal action has been taken.

World.title: Punjab's 'Business Class' programme helps over 20k student-led ventures garner Rs 90 cr revenue
World.content: NEW DELHI: Punjab's 'Business Class' programme, introduced under the state government's Sikhya Kranti initiative, has helped over 20,000 student-led ventures generate nearly Rs 90 crore in revenue within a year, Higher Education Minister Harjot Singh Bains said on Sunday.The programme, launched during the 2025-26 academic session, included a compulsory two-credit course for students pursuing B.Com, BBA, B.Tech and B.Voc courses, besides those studying in Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) and polytechnic colleges.According to the government, around 95,000 students from 925 higher and technical education institutions participated in the programme.Of these, 25,693 students started businesses, while 20,241 ventures generated nearly Rs 90 crore in revenue during the first year.Bains said the initiative aims to transform students from job seekers into entrepreneurs and employment generators."Our objective is not merely to award degrees but to nurture a generation of young innovators, entrepreneurs and job creators," he said in a statement.The minister further said the results demonstrate that young people can build businesses and contribute to the state's economy when provided with the right opportunities.Under Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann's leadership, Punjab's Sikhya Kranti is preparing youth "not just for the jobs of tomorrow, but to create tomorrow's opportunities," he said.The programme was implemented across 20 universities, 494 colleges, 320 ITIs and 91 polytechnic colleges.Unlike conventional classroom teaching, the course focuses on practical entrepreneurial skills, including identifying business opportunities, market validation, business setup, digital marketing, pricing, customer acquisition, financial planning and communication.The government said nearly 57,000 students, or about 60 per cent of participants, actively engaged in practical business activities during the academic session.Students launched ventures in sectors including e-commerce, food services, digital content creation, coding, graphic design, retail, beauty services, agriculture-based enterprises and handicrafts.Among the examples cited by the government were a matcha beverage startup by a Guru Nanak Dev University student, a digital career guidance platform developed by a student of Maharaja Ranjit Singh Punjab Technical University, an online jewellery business, a mushroom cultivation enterprise, a home-based nail art venture and an online electronics store.Encouraged by the programme's performance, vice-chancellors of universities across Punjab have recommended extending the course to all undergraduate programmes, including BA and BSc, from the 2026-27 academic session, the statement said.The government said the expansion is expected to equip a larger number of students with entrepreneurial skills alongside their regular academic studies.

World.title: Keep students focused on studies, away from protest calls: AIU to varsities
World.content:
AIU said prolonged protests could cause loss of academic time, disrupt preparation and create avoidable stress (representative image)

NEW DELHI: The Association of Indian Universities (AIU) has asked universities and higher education institutions to counsel students against staying away from classes to join protests over recent examination controversies, saying prolonged agitation comes at a âconsiderable costâ to their studies.In a letter to vice-chancellors and directors of member institutions, AIU president Vinay Kumar Pathak urged them to engage with students with empathy but ensure that their energies were not âdiverted by calls to protestâ.The July 21 letter comes amid continuing protests at Delhiâs Jantar Mantar over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. Students and other protesters have demanded examination reforms, accountability for the leak and the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.âIn the wake of recent concerns surrounding the conduct of certain national-level examinations, a section of students on several campuses has been staying away from classes to take part in protests and agitations â at considerable cost to their own studies,â Pathak said.While acknowledging that studentsâ concerns deserved to be heard âwith empathy and respectâ, the AIU said prolonged protests could cause loss of academic time, disrupt preparation and create avoidable stress.âProlonged agitation exacts its heaviest price from the students themselves â in lost academic time, disrupted preparation and avoidable stress,â the letter said.The AIU argued that this cost was unnecessary as the government was committed to resolving the concerns and had conducted the recent NEET examination in a âtransparent and error-free mannerâ. The June 21 examination was held after the original May 3 test was cancelled following a question-paper leak.âI would, therefore, earnestly appeal to you to counsel our students â with patience, sensitivity and care for their future â to remain focused on their academic pursuits and not to allow their energies to be diverted by calls to protest,â Pathak said.The association also asked students to repose faith in the governmentâs efforts to strengthen the examination system rather than be influenced by ârumour and speculationâ.âThe Honâble Prime Minister has himself appealed to students and has assured the nation that all possible steps will be taken to ensure that future examinations are conducted in a completely fair, transparent and secure manner,â the letter said.Pathak asked university heads to personally engage with students, mentor them and keep campuses âcalm and focusedâ.âI am confident that, with your personal attention and compassionate leadership, our campuses will remain calm and focused, and our students will devote their full energies to their studies and to nation-building,â he said.

World.title: Kerala UDF constituent IUML trains guns on Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar
World.content:
The Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) Wandoor constituency committee has openly expressed its dissatisfaction with Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar, the MLA representing the Wandoor Assembly constituency.

At a constituency-level meeting held recently, IUML leaders from panchayats across Wandoor accused Mr. Anil Kumar of sidelining the party after assuming office as Revenue Minister. They said the IUML and its workers had campaigned tirelessly for his victory when he contested the last Assembly election as the United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate.

Wandoor, a Scheduled Caste-reserved constituency, comprises the grama panchayats of Mampad, Wandoor, Thiruvali, Chokad, Kalikavu, Karuvarakundu, Thuvvoor, and Porur. Representatives from all these panchayats participated in the meeting and voiced their discontent over the Minister’s approach towards the IUML.

They alleged that the Minister had failed to engage with the IUML or acknowledge the contributions of its workers after taking the office. The leaders also accused him of failing to honour several commitments he had made ahead of the election.

The strongest criticism came from representatives of the Thiruvali panchayat, who alleged that the Minister had gone back on his assurance that a decision would be taken before April 30 on allotting the post of Thiruvali grama panchayat president to the IUML for one year.

Local IUML leaders also expressed concern over the future of their cooperation with Mr. Anil Kumar. Some warned that they would distance themselves from the Minister and refrain from participating in programmes associated with him unless their concerns were addressed.

World.title: BU manages surge in hostel admissions after commissioning new building with 58 rooms
World.content:
Bharathiar University has been able to manage with the surge in hostel admissions for the 2026-27 session owing to the inauguration of a new hostel at the start of this month. Constructed at a cost of ₹3 crore, the hostel named Vasuki has 58 rooms with a capacity to accommodate 246 students.

This time around, about 150 additional students were admitted into the hostels.

BU has, in all, 13 hostels named after poets and family members of Bharathiar. These 13 comprise four men’s hostels, five women’s hostels, a sports hostel, two hostels for research scholars and one international hostel.

The university prioritises hostel admission to students from far-off places. Till last year, the hostels accommodated close to 1400 students.

This time around, the women’s hostels are fully occupied. Likewise, the sports hostel and the hostels for men and women research scholars are also entirely occupied. The international hostel with an intake capacity of 45 is also in high demand, Registrar R. Rajavel said.

Undergraduates and postgraduate students are accommodated in rooms with capacity to accommodate two to four students. Factoring in the continuous surge in student patronage for its hostels, the Syndicate of Bharathiar University recently approved a proposal for sprucing up the building infrastructure.

World.title: Doctor in Kerala’s Kannur booked over alleged medical negligence, hospital denies charges
World.content:
The Kannur Town police have registered a case against a doctor at KIMS Sreechand Hospital after a patient alleged that she was discharged without the fish bone lodged in her throat being removed, resulting in prolonged pain and further surgery.

The case was been registered against Dr. Gaurav Baber, 35, following a complaint by P.V. Savithri, a resident of Echikkovil, Pilicode, in Kasaragod district.

In the complaint, Ms. Savithri said she was admitted to the hospital after a fish bone got stuck in her throat. Following an endoscopic procedure, doctors told her that the bone had been removed, and that she had been discharged. However, her throat pain persisted. Further treatment and a CT scan at the Pariyaram Government Medical College Hospital (MCH) revealed that another fish bone remained lodged in her throat. The retained bone was later surgically removed at the hospital.

The police said the case was registered after a preliminary inquiry into a complaint submitted by Ms. Savithiri to the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Kannur, alleging medical negligence and physical suffering caused by the treatment.

Responding to the allegations, the KIMS Sreechand Hospital authorities denied any medical negligence and said the incident had occured in February this year. According to the hospital, the patient underwent an endoscopic removal of the fish bone after an X-ray identified a foreign body in her throat.

The hospital said the treating gastroenterologist had advised a CT scan after the procedure, in line with the standard protocol, to confirm that no additional foreign body remained in the patient’s throat. However, the patient allegedly declined to undergo the scan citing financial constraints and took discharge against the doctor’s advice. She was also asked to return for review after two days.

Instead, the patient later sought treatment at the Kannur Government MCH, where a CT scan reportedly detected another fish bone, which was subsequently removed, said hospital administrator Muhammed Nabeel.

KIMS hospital maintained that no surgery was performed at the hospital, contrary to the complaint, and that only an endoscopic procedure had been done. The hospital said all procedures and medical records were fully documented, and that it had cooperated with the police investigation.

According to the hospital, the police had earlier heard the doctor’s explanation during the preliminary inquiry, and the management believes that the case is without merit. It alleged that the complaint was intended to tarnish the reputation of the hospital.

World.title: Why so selective on paper leaks, Nadda asks Rahul
World.content:
Union Minister J.P. Nadda on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) urged the Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, not to be “selective” in citing paper leak cases, saying that such a serious issue should not be exploited for political mileage. He said the government was ready for an in-depth discussion in Parliament, which he described as the most appropriate forum to collectively find lasting solutions.

At a late-evening press conference, Mr. Nadda said: “Students have raised concerns regarding paper leaks. I appeal that the issue should not be turned into a political matter, nor should anyone seek political gains from it. This is a grave problem, and it deserves a serious and in-depth discussion.”

He said the Bharatiya Janata Party-led NDA government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi was treating the issue with the utmost sincerity.

Reacting to Mr. Gandhi’s press briefing earlier in the day, the Union Minister said the LoP quoted a figure of about 150 instances of paper leaks. “These matters require investigation. This is a responsible government; every issue will be thoroughly examined and all the facts will be placed before the people,” he said.

Mr. Nadda said Mr. Gandhi did not mention incidents of paper leak and related irregularities reported under governments led by Opposition parties, including the Congress. Claiming that the list was much longer, Mr. Nadda said some of them had happened in Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Punjab, Kerala, and Karnataka.

“I want to ask the Leader of the Opposition: why are you being so selective? This shows that your objective is not the welfare of students Instead, you want to derive political mileage from students’ issues, which is unfortunate,” said Mr. Nadda.

He said rather than engaging in accusations and counter-accusations, the best forum to discuss the issue was Parliament. “We are ready for a detailed discussion to get to the root of the problem, identify the factors behind paper leaks, examine how the Union government has responded, and discuss how other governments should also tackle it,” the Union Minister said.

“The Opposition should not keep shifting the goalposts. We are not making any accusations against anyone. Children are the country’s future and it is the responsibility of both the government and the Opposition to safeguard their interests. We should come together to formulate a sound policy, find a permanent solution,” said Mr. Nadda.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh termed Mr. Nadda’s press conference “a sure sign of the regime’s increasing desperation.”

“The whole press conference was an unending series of ‘what-aboutery’. Mr. Nadda must go beyond such juvenile finger-pointing to first acknowledge the uniquely spectacular nature of the Mantri Pradhan’s and Pradhan Mantri’s failures,” Mr. Ramesh wrote on X.

‘Political tools’

Earlier, terming the ongoing protests in Delhi a matter of serious concern, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said that attempts were being made to “use the students and youth” as “political tools to serve their own political interests”. He said under Mr. Modi’s leadership, the government remained fully committed to fulfilling the aspirations of students and young people and ensuring their welfare.

“It is our responsibility to listen to every concern raised by our students and address it effectively. I am fully confident that India’s aware, mature and discerning youth can clearly see through such misleading attempts and will continue to choose the path of progress, development, and nation-building,” said Mr. Singh.

He said that despite the government expressing willingness to hold meaningful discussions on every issue in Parliament, the Opposition was trying to “seek solutions on the streets”. “If the Opposition is serious about these matters, it should refrain from disrupting the ongoing Monsoon Session and instead use Parliament to raise all issues and draw the country’s attention to them,” he said.

World.title: World Brain Day observed
World.content:
Centre for Neuroscience, Department of Biotechnology at Cochin University of Science and Technology (Cusat), observed World Brain Day on Tuesday (July 22, 2026) with a series of public awareness programmes on the theme ‘Healthy Brain for a Healthy Society'.

The event also marked the launch of the public outreach initiatives for the international conference on Translational Neuroscience to be held at the university from September 14 to 16, according to a release.

Music director Ouseppachan flagged off a memory walk on the occasion. Devadath Shaji, scriptwriter and filmmaker, delivered the keynote address, the release said.

World.title: Many farmers in Pochampalli SIPCOT not compensated according to records, says survey report
World.content:
As many as 76 farmers who contributed their land to the Pochampalli SIPCOT in Krishnagiri have been compensated only ₹14,000 to ₹17,000 per acre, instead of the ₹43,000 per acre as declared in the records of SIPCOT, according to a survey released here on Wednesday.

A total of 215 persons were interviewed in the survey conducted by the Forum for Indian Women Intellect (FIWI) in 18 villages adjacent to the SIPCOT complex.

Led by its founder and retired IAS officer P. Sivakami, the forum said there was a need to monitor and audit the SIPCOT complexes, as they affected the quality of life.

The survey said most of the respondents suffered from health issues such as respiratory distress, skin inflammation, and eye irritation due to the industrial smoke.

“Doctors at the nearby hospital confirmed that many people visited the facility daily for skin issues caused by the pollution,” Ms. Sivakami said.

The other concerns were water scarcity and degrading quality of groundwater. Though the residents had lodged complaints and protested against the environmental pollution, no action was taken by the State, the survey said. Since it was mostly women who were employed at the SIPCOT, they complained of knee pain as they had to work standing up for over 12 hours.

The survey also said that out of the 147 units in SIPCOT, only 45 units were operational, while the other 50 were under construction. “As a large extent of land lies vacant and many people in the village are unemployed, the State could look at setting up cottage industries or processing units for coconut coir, mango pulp, and tomato puree,” the survey said.

It also recommended that medical infrastructure be arranged, with special attention to respiratory issues and weekly medical camps.

The survey also demanded a law to provide 75% of employment to local people and the abolition of the temporary contract system.

World.title: Piracy fails to dampen advance bookings for Chief Minister Vijay’s Jana Nayagan
World.content:
Despite having been leaked online ahead of its theatrical release, Jana Nayagan, starring Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay, has witnessed strong advance ticket sales across Chennai and its neighbouring districts, though the response has been mixed in other parts of Tamil Nadu.

While some cinemas reported a full house over the weekend, others said bookings were highest for the opening day, with Friday witnessing a comparatively low demand. Cinema owners added that bookings had been driven largely by members of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), youngsters associated with Mr. Vijay’s fan club, and Gen Z movie-goers.

‘First show’ tickets had been sold for as high as ₹500 to ₹700 in certain pockets of the State.

“The film will have a bumper opening as it is Chief Minister Vijay’s last film. The bookings have been phenomenal. The bookings have been good in Kerala, too,” film industry analyst Sreedhar Pillai said.

“The film has received an ‘A’ certificate from the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC). This means children will not be allowed to watch it. Mr. Vijay’s fan base has traditionally been children and families.” Mr. Pillai added. Multiplexes, in particular, have always enforced the certification norms and they do not allow minors to enter screenings.

P. Dinesh Kumar, proprietor of Guru Theatre in Madurai, said, “Bookings are looking good until Sunday. People in Madurai are doubly excited to watch the movie. They come to cinemas for the experience and the atmosphere, which cannot be replicated online.”

The response from cinema owners in Madurai and Tiruchi regions was similar. S. Kumar, Relationship Manager of Broadway Cinemas Coimbatore, said bookings had been good so far.

“Jana Nayagan has generated extraordinary excitement among audiences. The response in Tamil Nadu has been particularly remarkable, with tickets sold out for the opening weekend in cinemas across the State. With over 3 lakh advance bookings already sold, we are witnessing an exceptionally strong momentum across key markets nationwide,” said Sanjeev Kumar Bijli, Executive Director, PVR INOX Limited.

According to data shared by trade tracker Sacnilk (on its web portal), Jana Nayagan has sold 7.37 lakh tickets nationwide, and grossed ₹16.78 crore in advance bookings across 9,566 shows.

Revenue-sharing row

On Wednesday night, some cinemas in Chennai and in certain towns said they would not screen Jana Nayagan, citing disagreements with distributors over sharing of revenue.

“For Tamil cinema, last-minute release day disputes have almost become routine. From revenue sharing arrangements to screening terms, disagreements between distributors and exhibitors have often cast a shadow over big-ticket releases, before being resolved at the eleventh hour,” said a cinema owner in Salem. Sources in the industry hinted that distributors were asking for a 70%-75% share, rather than the usual 65%-70%.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Heavy security deployed at Jantar Mantar, as crowd of protesters swells
World.content:
The chants grew louder and the crowd thicker at Jantar Mantar on Wednesday (July 22, 2026) as fresh groups of protesters from across the country poured into the protest site, many after overnight journeys by bus and train.

Also read: Police file four FIRs amid flak over crackdown on protesters

Two days after the ‘Chalo Sansad’ march, the sit-in continued to draw new participants, many walking into the protest site with backpacks and rolled-up banners after travelling through the night. Volunteers directed them towards seating areas and distributed drinking water and food packets as more groups joined the gathering.

The issue of NEET paper leak and police crackdown on protesters at Jantar Mantar and neighbouring areas rocked both Houses of Parliament on Wednesday (July 22, 2026). The government offered an elaborate discussion on the issue and accused the opposition of not allowing a debate by disrupting proceedings.

Also read: Hundreds of people order food online for protestors at Jantar Mantar

Activist Sonam Wangchuk said he would end his indefinite hunger strike if the Centre gives an unequivocal assurance that no punitive or retaliatory action would be taken against students and youth who participated in the protest against alleged examination irregularities.
